---
title: "Reproducing the 2017 Economist visual styleguide"
---

```{r, include = FALSE}
## ragg writes plain sRGB PNGs; the macOS default device embeds a profile that darkens colors.
knitr::opts_chunk$set(comment = "#>", dpi = 192, dev = "ragg_png")
## Fold each chunk's code behind a "Code" toggle; output stays visible.
local({
  source_hook <- knitr::knit_hooks$get("source")
  knitr::knit_hooks$set(source = function(x, options) {
    paste0("\n\n<details><summary>Code</summary>\n\n", source_hook(x, options), "\n\n</details>\n\n")
  })
})
```

This article reproduces the charts of [The Economist visual styleguide](https://sa.ipaa.org.au/wp-content/uploads/2026/02/Economist-CHARTstyleguide_20170505.pdf) (Version 1.2, 4 May 2017, by Matt McLean) with *ggthemes*, using `theme_economist_2017()`, `economist_2017_pal()`, `guide_axis_economist_2017()` and `economist_2017_chart()`.

Block quotes are the guide's own words, with its spelling and typos.

The 2017 style guide was an update of the "classic" economist chart style. 
["Mistakes, "we've drawn a few"](https://www.reddit.com/r/dataisbeautiful/comments/b6g2v8/economist_mistakes_weve_drawn_a_few/) describes the thinking behind the changes.

```{r setup, message = FALSE}
library(ggthemes)
library(ggplot2)
library(grid)
library(gtable)

## The guide's own colour values, as shipped with the package.
print_pal <- ggthemes_data$economist_2017$print
web_pal <- ggthemes_data$economist_2017$web
swatch <- function(name) print_pal$swatches$value[print_pal$swatches$name == name]

econ_red <- print_pal$accent
print_bg <- print_pal$ground
print_highlight <- print_pal$highlight
print_numberbox <- print_pal$number_box
grid_col <- print_pal$grid

## Color orders per chart type.
pal_bar <- economist_2017_pal("print", type = "bar_side")
pal_stack <- economist_2017_pal("print", type = "stacked")
pal_line <- economist_2017_pal("print", type = "line_side")
pal_dot <- economist_2017_pal("print", type = "dot")
pal_pie <- economist_2017_pal("print", type = "pie")

## The aesthetics of the helper functions below are columns of their data.
.data <- rlang::.data

## Each chunk names a size (`econ_size`, `econ_height`); the hook sets the figure size.
knitr::opts_chunk$set(econ_size = "one_column")
knitr::opts_hooks$set(econ_size = function(options) {
  ## Chunks that draw no figure name no height, and keep knitr's defaults.
  size <- tryCatch(economist_2017_size(options$econ_size, options$econ_height), error = function(e) NULL)
  if (is.null(size)) {
    return(options)
  }
  options$fig.width <- size[["width"]]
  options$fig.height <- size[["height"]]
  options$out.width <- paste0(round(size[["width"]] * 96), "px")
  options
})


## Set the labels of some categories in bold.
bold_label <- function(which) {
  function(x) as.expression(lapply(x, function(l) if (l %in% which) bquote(bold(.(l))) else l))
}

no_value_axis <- function() {
  theme(
    axis.text.x = element_blank(),
    axis.ticks.x = element_blank(),
    axis.line.x = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.major = element_blank()
  )
}
```

## Chart sizes

In print, charts come in fixed print widths, in points. Only the leader block and the Espresso lead image have a fixed height.  The theme, `theme_economist_2017()`, derives the relative scaling of plot elements from the absolute numbers, but allows them to scale with `base_size`, the size of the axis labels. The guide's own numbers are at `base_size = 7`, the guide's axis-label size, which is what every chart here uses.

```{r sizes-table}
options(knitr.kable.NA = "")
sizes <- ggthemes_data$economist_2017$sizes
knitr::kable(
  data.frame(
    Size = sizes$label,
    `Name` = paste0("`", sizes$size, "`"),
    `Width (pt)` = sizes$width,
    `Height (pt)` = sizes$height,
    `Web width (px)` = sizes$web_width,
    `Web height (px)` = sizes$web_height,
    check.names = FALSE
  )
)
```

`economist_2017_size()` returns a chart size as `c(width =, height =)`, in inches by default or in points. 
Figures are shown at actual size: a one-column chart, 160pt, is 213px wide.

```{r size-example}
economist_2017_size("one_column", height = 165)
economist_2017_size("leader", units = "pt")
```



## Typefaces

Economist charts in this era use the proprietary Econ Sans and its condensed cut, Econ Sans Cnd. 
Since Econ Sans is not public, `economist_2017_font()` picks the closest installed substitute as the `base_family`: Fira Sans Condensed, then Roboto Condensed, then `"sans"`.

The data element `ggthemes_data$economist_2017$typefaces` records what each is for and how ggthemes draws it.

```{r typefaces-table}
typefaces <- ggthemes_data$economist_2017$typefaces
knitr::kable(
  data.frame(
    Typeface = typefaces$typeface,
    Weight = typefaces$weight,
    Use = typefaces$use,
    `Drawn as` = typefaces$face,
    `Theme elements` = ifelse(
      is.na(typefaces$elements) | typefaces$elements == "",
      "",
      paste0("`", gsub(", ", "`, `", typefaces$elements), "`")
    ),
    check.names = FALSE
  )
)
```


Economist charts often use footnotes, identified by an ordered set of stymbols.

```{r footnote-symbols}
economist_2017_footnote(1:8)
```

```{r footnote-figure, econ_size = "two_column", econ_height = 75}
## The label on the left over a rule, the eight symbols on the right.
slate <- "#67818E"
symbols <- data.frame(x = 0.36 + 0.08 * (0:7), number = 1:8, symbol = economist_2017_footnote(1:8))

footnote_figure <- ggplot(symbols, aes(x, 0)) +
  annotate("segment", x = 0, xend = 1, y = 1.15, yend = 1.15, colour = slate, linewidth = 0.2) +
  annotate("text", x = 0, y = 0.55, label = "Footnote symbols", hjust = 0, vjust = 1, fontface = "bold",
           colour = slate, size = 7.5 / ggplot2::.pt) +
  annotate("text", x = 0, y = 0.05, label = "order of use", hjust = 0, vjust = 1, colour = slate,
           size = 7.5 / ggplot2::.pt) +
  ## Superscript digits above 3 are missing from many fonts, so use a small raised numeral.
  geom_text(aes(label = number), size = 7 / ggplot2::.pt, hjust = 1, vjust = 0, nudge_y = 0.05, colour = slate) +
  geom_text(aes(x = x + 0.006, label = symbol), size = 14 / ggplot2::.pt, hjust = 0, vjust = 0.5, nudge_y = -0.3) +
  scale_x_continuous(limits = c(0, 1), expand = c(0, 0)) +
  scale_y_continuous(limits = c(-1, 1.8), expand = c(0, 0)) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = NULL) +
  theme_economist_2017("print", base_size = 7) +
  theme(
    axis.text = element_blank(), axis.ticks = element_blank(), axis.line = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.major = element_blank()
  )

economist_2017_chart(footnote_figure, media = "print")
```

## Anatomy of a chart

The value axis sits on the right, with each label just above its gridline inside the panel. `scale_y_continuous(position = "right")` and `guide_axis_economist_2017()` produce this setup. `ggplot` themes do not allow placing
a label *above* an axis, which is why `guide_axis_economist_2017()` is required.

```{r anatomy-bare, econ_height = 165}
## Monthly yields, in years since the start.
tokyo_x <- c(1, seq(1.25, 13.5, by = 0.25), 13.7)
bonds <- data.frame(
  year = rep(tokyo_x, 2),
  yield = c(
    4.7, 5.0, 5.2, 5.1, 5.6, 6.6, 6.7, 7.9, 6.8, 6.5, 6.7, 6.2, 5.7, 5.5, 5.4, 4.9, 4.6, 4.2, 4.5, 4.0,
    3.4, 3.9, 4.1, 4.5, 4.5, 3.9, 3.0, 3.0, 2.9, 3.2, 3.2, 2.9, 2.5, 2.5, 2.6, 2.1, 1.9, 1.8, 1.6, 1.1,
    1.5, 1.8, 1.6, 1.8, 1.8, 1.8, 1.7, 1.9, 1.6, 1.2, 1.2, 1.25,
    4.7, 5.2, 5.8, 5.9, 6.3, 6.2, 6.2, 5.8, 5.4, 5.0, 5.3, 4.7, 4.9, 5.2, 4.8, 4.0, 4.0, 3.8, 3.6, 4.3,
    4.2, 4.2, 4.6, 4.1, 4.2, 4.4, 4.1, 4.3, 4.4, 4.8, 5.1, 4.7, 4.6, 4.6, 5.0, 4.5, 4.0, 3.6, 4.0, 3.7,
    2.7, 2.8, 3.6, 3.4, 3.6, 3.7, 3.2, 2.6, 3.1, 3.4, 3.0, 2.3
  ),
  period = rep(c("January 1989 (Japan)", "January 1999 (US)"), each = length(tokyo_x))
)

tokyo <- ggplot(bonds, aes(year, yield, colour = period)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.8) +
  scale_y_continuous(
    guide = guide_axis_economist_2017(), position = "right", limits = c(0, 8), breaks = seq(0, 8, 2), expand = c(0, 0)
  ) +
  scale_x_continuous(
    limits = c(1, 13.7), breaks = 1:13, labels = ifelse(1:13 %in% c(1, 5, 10, 13), 1:13, ""), expand = c(0, 0)
  ) +
  scale_colour_economist_2017("print", type = "line_side") +
  labs(
    title = "Where Tokyo leads",
    subtitle = "Ten-year government-bond yields, %",
    x = "Years since start", y = NULL, colour = "Period beginning:"
  ) +
  ## The fallback font is wider, so the keys take two rows.
  guides(colour = guide_legend(nrow = 2)) +
  theme_economist_2017("print", base_size = 7)

tokyo
```

The theme sets the guide's type and rules: 9.5pt bold title, 8pt subtitle, 7.5pt legend labels, 7pt axis labels, 0.5pt gridlines, a 6.5pt source line (`labs(caption = )`), and ticks hanging below the baseline.

Three features of Economist charts are not theme elements:

* the **red tab**, 15pt by 5pt, above the title;
* for web charts, a **red rule** across the full width, with the key beside the title;
* a 10pt by 1pt **red marker** above each panel heading.

The function `economist_2017_chart()` adds them to a finished plot and returns a grob you can print or save.

```{r anatomy-chart, econ_height = 165}
economist_2017_chart(
  tokyo + labs(caption = "Source: Thomson Reuters"),
  media = "print"
)
```

## Source, footnote and number box

The print chart sits on a pale blue ground. The web chart sits on white under a red rule, with the key beside the title.

```{r anatomy-print, econ_height = 165}
fn <- economist_2017_footnote(1:2)

economist_2017_chart(
  tokyo +
    labs(
      subtitle = paste0("Ten-year government-bond yields", fn[1], ", %"),
      caption = "Source: Thomson Reuters"
    ),
  media = "print",
  footnote = paste0(fn[1], "Annualised")
)
```

```{r anatomy-web, econ_size = "two_column", econ_height = 190}
## Olympic medal sweeps; the 1996 games had none.
sweeps <- data.frame(
  year = c(1948, 1952, 1956, 1960, 1964, 1968, 1972, 1976, 1980, 1984, 1988, 1992, 2000, 2004, 2008, 2012, 2016),
  us = c(5, 6, 6, 4, 4, 6, 2, 4, 0, 1, 2, 1, 0, 2, 3, 0, 1),
  ussr = c(0, 4, 1, 4, 0, 0, 2, 3, 5, 0, 3, 1, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0),
  eg = c(0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 6, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0),
  other = c(2, 0, 3, 0, 0, 1, 4, 2, 0, 0, 3, 3, 2, 2, 4, 2, 0)
)
sweeps <- data.frame(
  year = rep(sweeps$year, 4),
  count = c(sweeps$other, sweeps$eg, sweeps$ussr, sweeps$us),
  country = factor(
    rep(c("Other", "East Germany", "Soviet Union", "United States"), each = nrow(sweeps)),
    levels = c("United States", "Soviet Union", "East Germany", "Other")
  )
)

anthem <- ggplot(sweeps, aes(year, count, fill = country)) +
  geom_col(width = 2.7, position = position_stack(reverse = TRUE)) +
  annotate("text", x = 1992, y = 1.55, label = "*", colour = "white", size = 7 / ggplot2::.pt) +
  ## Blue1, red1 and blue2, with the lightest grey step for "Other".
  scale_fill_manual(
    values = c("United States" = swatch("blue1"),
               "Soviet Union" = swatch("red1"),
               "East Germany" = swatch("blue2"),
               "Other" = web_pal$sequential$grey[1])
  ) +
  scale_y_continuous(
    guide = guide_axis_economist_2017(), position = "right", limits = c(0, 12), breaks = seq(0, 12, 2), expand = c(0, 0)
  ) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(1948, 2016, 4), labels = economist_2017_year_format(), expand = c(0.01, 0)) +
  guides(fill = guide_legend(ncol = 2)) +
  labs(
    title = "National anthem monopolies", subtitle = "Number of “medal sweeps” by country",
    x = NULL, y = NULL, fill = NULL,
    caption = "Sources: International Olympic Committee;\nSports Reference; The Economist"
  ) +
  theme_economist_2017("web", base_size = 7)

economist_2017_chart(anthem, media = "web", footnote = "*Unified team of ex-Soviet republics")
```

## Type scale and margins

The default theme is the standard chart: print, web, Espresso article-body charts and the frame of panel charts.

| Element | Standard size / leading | Theme element |
|---|---:|---|
| Headline | 9.5 / 11pt | `plot.title` |
| Subtitle | 8 / 9.5pt | `plot.subtitle` |
| Legend and panel heading | 7.5 / 9pt | `legend.text`, `strip.text` |
| Axis numbers | 7 / 9pt | `axis.text` |
| Axis title | 7 / 7.5pt | `axis.title` |
| Source | 6.5pt | `plot.caption` |

Standard print charts have 6pt outer margins; standard web charts have none. Panel charts keep the 6pt margin and put 24pt between panels.

Leader blocks and Espresso lead images use smaller type. Leader blocks: 8pt headlines, 7pt subtitles, 6pt axis text. Espresso: 8pt headlines and subtitles, 7.5pt detail text.

### Leader block

```{r dimensions-leader, econ_size = "leader"}
## Monthly, January 2011 to mid-2015.
leader_data <- data.frame(
  year = c(2011.02, 2011 + (1:55) / 12),
  change = c(
    1.47, 1.56, 1.85, 2.19, 2.58, 2.69, 2.72, 2.81, 2.88, 2.84, 2.73, 2.61, 2.54, 2.54, 2.45, 2.19,
    1.85, 1.62, 1.52, 1.49, 1.63, 1.82, 1.82, 1.67, 1.59, 1.61, 1.52, 1.25, 1.22, 1.42, 1.57, 1.51,
    1.31, 1.12, 1.13, 1.3, 1.4, 1.25, 1.24, 1.51, 1.71, 1.73, 1.7, 1.64, 1.53, 1.45, 1.28, 0.98,
    0.51, 0.21, 0.27, 0.22, 0.2, 0.29, 0.32, 0.33
  )
)
leader <- ggplot(leader_data, aes(year, change)) +
  geom_line(colour = pal_line(1), linewidth = 0.5) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 2, colour = econ_red, linewidth = 0.2) +
  annotate("text", x = 2015.95, y = 2.08, label = "Fed target  2", hjust = 1, vjust = 0,
           colour = econ_red, size = 6 / ggplot2::.pt) +
  scale_y_continuous(
    guide = guide_axis_economist_2017(), position = "right", limits = c(0, 3), breaks = c(0, 1, 3), expand = c(0, 0)
  ) +
  ## A tick at each year, with the last marking the end of the data.
  scale_x_continuous(
    limits = c(2011, 2016), breaks = c(2011:2015, 2015.57), labels = c(economist_2017_year(2011:2015), ""),
    expand = c(0, 0)
  ) +
  labs(title = "US consumer prices", subtitle = "% increase on a year earlier",
       x = NULL, y = NULL) +
  theme_economist_2017("print", base_size = 7) +
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(size = rel(0.8), lineheight = 1),
    plot.subtitle = element_text(size = rel(0.7), lineheight = 1),
    axis.text = element_text(size = rel(0.6), lineheight = 1),
    axis.text.x = element_text(hjust = 0),
    axis.title = element_text(size = rel(0.6), lineheight = 1),
    plot.caption = element_text(size = rel(0.6)),
    plot.margin = margin(6, 6, 5, 6, "pt")
  )

economist_2017_chart(
  leader,
  media = "print",
  tab = c(15, 4)
)
```

### Espresso lead image

```{r dimensions-espresso, econ_size = "espresso"}
espresso_data <- data.frame(
  year = 2007:2015,
  change = c(4, 2, -5.7, 4.4, 6.8, 4.1, 2.9, 3, 0.9)
)
espresso <- ggplot(espresso_data, aes(year, change)) +
  geom_col(fill = pal_bar(1), width = 0.67) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, colour = econ_red, linewidth = 0.2) +
  scale_y_continuous(
    guide = guide_axis_economist_2017(), position = "right", limits = c(-8, 8), breaks = seq(-8, 8, 4), expand = c(0, 0)
  ) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = 2007:2015, labels = economist_2017_year_format()) +
  labs(title = "US retail sales",
       subtitle = "Excluding motor vehicles and parts,\n% change on a year earlier",
       x = NULL, y = NULL) +
  theme_economist_2017("print", base_size = 7) +
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(size = rel(0.8), lineheight = 1),
    plot.subtitle = element_text(size = rel(0.8), lineheight = 1),
    axis.text = element_text(size = rel(0.75), lineheight = 9 / 7.5),
    axis.title = element_text(size = rel(0.75), lineheight = 9 / 7.5),
    plot.caption = element_text(size = rel(0.75)),
    ## 120pt of chart, then 40pt blank; the bottom margin keeps the ground under the spacer.
    plot.margin = margin(6, 6, 6 + 40, 6, "pt")
  )

economist_2017_chart(
  espresso +
    labs(caption = "Source: US Department of Commerce"),
  media = "print"
)
```

### Panel chart

Landscape panel charts are two columns wide, with the panels side by side, 24pt apart:

```{r dimensions-panel, econ_size = "two_column", econ_height = 195}
## The "Racy" chart: daily lines on the left, 12 points on the right.
panel_names <- c(
  "Donald Trump’s media dominance\nand polling surge",
  "Support for Trump v racial resentment\nand authoritarianism†,\nRepublican primary voters"
)
tv_mentions <- c(
  34, 29, 26, 35, 47, 56, 58, 55, 61, 64, 59, 55, 52, 52, 55, 58, 62, 61, 61, 58, 52, 50, 48, 53, 47, 41,
  41, 43, 42, 43, 47, 47, 48, 45, 35, 27, 27, 27, 27, 28, 37, 48, 50, 49, 57, 67, 63, 53, 55, 58, 56, 56,
  57, 57, 54, 54, 58, 57, 54, 45, 35, 35, 43, 48, 49, 53, 60, 64, 60, 60, 62, 69, 71, 69, 72, 70, 67, 69,
  71, 71, 71, 68, 70
)
polling <- c(
  3.8, 3.8, 4.1, 5.2, 6.2, 6.4, 9.3, 13, 16.7, 18.1, 19.3, 21.6, 23.6, 23.7, 22.5, 22.2, 22, 22.5, 24.4,
  26.5, 27.6, 28.8, 29.9, 30.4, 28, 24.8, 23.4, 23, 23.1, 23.4, 23.4, 24.8, 26.7, 27, 26.9, 25.7, 24.8,
  24.8, 24.5, 24.4, 26.1, 27.8, 28.6, 29.5, 29.8, 30.2, 31.6, 33.8, 34.5, 36, 35.5, 34.9, 34.6, 34.5,
  34.5, 34.7, 34.7, 35.7, 35.6, 34, 30.8, 29.3, 31.1, 33.6, 33.4, 33.9, 35.3, 36.2, 36.2, 34.1, 34.8,
  39.4, 42.9, 42.3, 41.4, 40.2, 39.3, 39.7, 40.4, 40.7, 42.2, 43.6, 45.3
)
days <- (6 * seq_along(tv_mentions) - 22) / 1.57
panel_data <- rbind(
  data.frame(panel = panel_names[1], x = days, series = "TV mentions", value = tv_mentions),
  ## The polling average has its own 0-50 axis, so it is drawn at twice its value.
  data.frame(panel = panel_names[1], x = days, series = "Polling average", value = 2 * polling),
  data.frame(
    panel = panel_names[2], x = 1:12, series = "Authoritarianism",
    value = c(43.5, 42.9, 42.6, 43.5, 44.4, 45.3, 46.4, 47.7, 48.9, 49.9, 50.4, 50.6)
  ),
  data.frame(
    panel = panel_names[2], x = 1:12, series = "Racial resentment",
    value = c(2, 9.5, 17.3, 24.9, 31.4, 35.3, 39.1, 43, 46.5, 50, 53.5, 56)
  )
)
panel_data$panel <- factor(panel_data$panel, levels = panel_names)

## Lettering around the axes, in each panel's data units.
slate <- "#67818E"
teal <- pal_line(2)[2]
maroon <- pal_line(4)[4]
panel_plot <- function(panel_pt) {
  up1 <- 100 / panel_pt # data units of the first panel per point
  up2 <- 60 / panel_pt
  txt <- function(data, size = 7.5) {
    geom_text(
      data = data, aes(.data$x, .data$y, label = .data$label, hjust = .data$hjust), colour = data$colour,
      size = size / ggplot2::.pt, inherit.aes = FALSE
    )
  }
  lab <- function(panel, x, y, label, hjust = 0.5, colour = "black") {
    data.frame(panel = factor(panel_names[panel], levels = panel_names), x = x, y = y, label = label,
               hjust = hjust, colour = colour)
  }
  axis_labels <- rbind(
    lab(1, -49.6, seq(0, 100, 20) + 4 * up1, seq(0, 100, 20), hjust = 0, colour = teal),
    lab(1, 342, seq(0, 100, 20) + 4 * up1, seq(0, 50, 10), hjust = 1, colour = maroon),
    lab(2, 13.7, seq(0, 60, 20) + 4 * up2, seq(0, 60, 20), hjust = 1)
  )
  unit_labels <- rbind(
    lab(1, -49.6, 100 + 13 * up1, "TV mentions*, % of total", hjust = 0, colour = teal),
    lab(1, 342, 100 + 13 * up1, "Polling average, %", hjust = 1, colour = maroon),
    lab(2, 13.7, 60 + 13 * up2, "Voter support, %", hjust = 1)
  )
  months <- lab(
    1, c(-4.4, 15.3, 46, 76.3, 105.5, 135.4, 165, 195, 226, 255.5, 285, 307.6), -9.5 * up1,
    c("J", "J", "A", "S", "O", "N", "D", "J", "F", "M", "A", "M")
  )
  years <- lab(1, c(86, 243), -19 * up1, c("2015", "2016"))
  direct_labels <- lab(2, c(1.2, 6.8), c(50, 32.5), c("Authoritarianism", "Racial resentment"), hjust = 0)
  scale_labels <- rbind(
    lab(2, 0.33, -9 * up2, "LOWEST", hjust = 0, colour = slate),
    lab(2, 12, -9 * up2, "HIGHEST", colour = slate)
  )
  scale_text <- lab(
    2, 7, c(-4.5, -13.5) * up2, c("Degree of authoritarianism", "Level of resentment"), colour = slate
  )
  scale_arrow <- data.frame(
    panel = factor(panel_names[2], levels = panel_names), x = 3.6, xend = 10.2, y = -9 * up2
  )
  ggplot(panel_data, aes(.data$x, .data$value, colour = .data$series)) +
    geom_line(linewidth = 0.8, show.legend = FALSE) +
    txt(axis_labels, 7) +
    txt(unit_labels) +
    txt(months, 7) +
    txt(years, 7) +
    txt(direct_labels) +
    txt(scale_labels, 6.5) +
    txt(scale_text, 6.5) +
    geom_segment(
      data = scale_arrow, aes(x = .data$x, xend = .data$xend, y = .data$y, yend = .data$y), colour = slate,
      linewidth = 0.3, arrow = grid::arrow(ends = "both", length = unit(3, "pt"), type = "closed"),
      inherit.aes = FALSE
    ) +
    facet_wrap(~panel, nrow = 1, scales = "free") +
    coord_cartesian(clip = "off", expand = FALSE) +
    ## Set the panel ranges so the lettering outside the axes does not stretch them.
    scale_x_continuous(
      limits = function(limits) if (diff(limits) > 100) c(-49.6, 342) else c(0.326, 13.7), oob = scales::oob_keep,
      breaks = function(limits) {
        if (limits[2] > 100) c(-9, 0, 31, 62, 92, 123, 153, 184, 215, 244, 275, 305) else c(1, 12)
      },
      labels = function(breaks) rep("", length(breaks))
    ) +
    scale_y_continuous(
      limits = function(limits) if (max(limits) > 80) c(0, 100) else c(0, 60), oob = scales::oob_keep,
      position = "right",
      breaks = function(limits) seq(0, limits[2], 20)) +
    scale_colour_manual(values = c(
      "TV mentions" = teal, "Polling average" = maroon, "Authoritarianism" = teal, "Racial resentment" = pal_line(1)
    )) +
    labs(title = "Racy", subtitle = "United States", x = " ", y = NULL) +
    theme_economist_2017("print", base_size = 7) +
    theme(axis.text.y = element_blank(), strip.text = element_text(margin = margin(3.5, 0, 18, 0)))
}
panel_chart <- panel_plot(60)

stopifnot(
  convertUnit(theme_economist_2017("print", base_size = 7)$panel.spacing.x, "pt", valueOnly = TRUE) == 24
)
economist_2017_chart(
  panel_chart +
    labs(caption = "Sources: GDELT; RCP; YouGov"),
  media = "print",
  footnote = paste0(
    "*National news mentions of Trump compared\nwith all Republican candidates ",
    "\u2020Poll Jul 30th-Aug 6th 2016"
  )
)
```

Portrait panel charts are one column wide, with the panels stacked 15pt apart.

```{r dimensions-panel-portrait, econ_height = 350}
stopifnot(
  convertUnit(theme_economist_2017("print", base_size = 7)$panel.spacing.y, "pt", valueOnly = TRUE) == 15
)
economist_2017_chart(
  panel_plot(68) +
    facet_wrap(~panel, ncol = 1, scales = "free", axes = "all") +
    labs(caption = "Sources: GDELT;\nRCP; YouGov"),
  media = "print",
  footnote = paste0(
    "*National news mentions of\nTrump compared with all\nRepublican candidates\n",
    "†Poll Jul 30th-Aug 6th 2016"
  )
)
```

## Color

The print palette is specified in CMYK and the web palette in hex. Both are in `ggthemes_data$economist_2017`.

The guide doesn't specify 1-1 colors for the web or separate color scales for print and web. The package only provides
single sets of color palettes to use with either web or print backgrounds.

```{r swatches, econ_size = "two_column", econ_height = 260}
## The palettes, grouped as the guide groups them.
qual <- print_pal$qualitative
by_name <- function(set, nm) setNames(set$value, set$name)[nm]
swatch_rows <- list(
  list("MAIN", c(
    "Econ red" = print_pal$accent, "Red1" = swatch("red1"), "Red text" = swatch("red text"),
    by_name(qual$bar_side, "blue1"), by_name(qual$bar_side, "blue2"), "Blue2 text" = swatch("blue2 text")
  )),
  list("SECONDARY", c(
    by_name(qual$bar_side, c("gold", "maroon", "mauve", "teal")), by_name(qual$stacked, "mint")
  )),
  list("BRIGHT, DARK", c(
    setNames(qual$bright$value, qual$bright$name), setNames(qual$dark$value, c("navy", "dk teal", "olive"))
  )),
  list("BACKGROUND", c("Print bkgd" = print_pal$ground, "Highlight" = print_highlight, "Number box" = print_numberbox)),
  list("NEUTRAL", c(
    "Grid lines" = grid_col, "Grey box" = swatch("grey box"), "Grey text" = swatch("grey text"),
    "Black 25" = swatch("black 25"), "Black 50" = swatch("black 50"), "Black 75" = swatch("black 75"),
    "Black" = swatch("black 100")
  )),
  list("WEB MAIN", with(web_pal$swatches[web_pal$swatches$group == "main", ], setNames(value, name))),
  list("WEB NEUTRAL", with(web_pal$swatches[web_pal$swatches$group == "neutral", ], setNames(value, name)))
)
swatch_data <- do.call(rbind, lapply(seq_along(swatch_rows), function(r) {
  hex <- swatch_rows[[r]][[2]]
  data.frame(group = swatch_rows[[r]][[1]], row = r, col = seq_along(hex), name = toupper(names(hex)), hex = hex)
}))

ggplot(swatch_data, aes(col, -row)) +
  geom_tile(aes(fill = hex), width = 0.94, height = 0.42) +
  geom_text(aes(y = -row + 0.36, label = name), size = 4 / ggplot2::.pt, vjust = 0) +
  geom_text(aes(y = -row - 0.32, label = hex), size = 4 / ggplot2::.pt, vjust = 1) +
  geom_text(
    data = unique(swatch_data[c("group", "row")]), aes(x = -1.5, y = -row, label = group),
    size = 6 / ggplot2::.pt, fontface = "bold", hjust = 0, inherit.aes = FALSE
  ) +
  scale_fill_identity() +
  scale_x_continuous(limits = c(-1.5, 9.5), expand = c(0, 0)) +
  labs(title = "Chart palette, print and web", x = NULL, y = NULL) +
  theme_economist_2017("web", base_size = 7) +
  theme(
    axis.text = element_blank(), axis.ticks = element_blank(), axis.line = element_blank(),
    panel.grid = element_blank()
  )
```

Each chart type has its own color order, chosen with the `type` argument of `economist_2017_pal()`.

Nine "equal lightness colour scales" come from the web palettes: `economist_2017_gradient_pal(hue)`, `scale_fill_economist_2017_c(hue)` and `scale_colour_economist_2017_c(hue)` use them.

```{r gradients, econ_size = "two_column", econ_height = 170}
## One column per hue, one row per step, darkest at the top.
hues <- names(web_pal$sequential)
steps <- do.call(rbind, lapply(seq_along(hues), function(i) {
  hex <- rev(web_pal$sequential[[hues[i]]])
  data.frame(col = i, step = seq_along(hex), hex = hex)
}))

ggplot(steps, aes(col, -step, fill = hex)) +
  geom_tile(width = 0.94, height = 0.58) +
  geom_text(aes(y = -step - 0.4, label = hex), size = 4.3 / ggplot2::.pt, vjust = 1) +
  scale_fill_identity() +
  scale_x_continuous(expand = c(0.01, 0)) +
  scale_y_continuous(expand = c(0, 0), limits = c(-6.9, -0.6)) +
  labs(title = "Equal lightness colour scales ", x = NULL, y = NULL) +
  theme_economist_2017("web", base_size = 7) +
  theme(
    axis.text = element_blank(), axis.ticks = element_blank(),
    axis.line = element_blank(), panel.grid = element_blank(),
    plot.margin = margin(0, 6, 3.5, 6)
  )
```

## Bar / column, side by side

### One trace

```{r african-lion, econ_height = 165}
ethiopia <- data.frame(
  year = 2004:2015,
  growth = c(11.7, 12.7, 11.5, 11.8, 11.2, 10.0, 10.6, 11.4, 8.7, 9.8, 10.3, 8.7)
)

lion <- ggplot(ethiopia, aes(year, growth)) +
  geom_col(fill = pal_bar(1), width = 0.6) +
  scale_y_continuous(
    guide = guide_axis_economist_2017(), position = "right", limits = c(0, 14), breaks = seq(0, 14, 2),
    expand = expansion(0)
  ) +
  ## Labels every other year, then the estimate; a tick for every year.
  scale_x_continuous(
    breaks = c(seq(2004, 2014, 2), 2015), labels = c("2004", "06", "08", "10", "12", "14", "15*"),
    minor_breaks = 2004:2015, guide = guide_axis(minor.ticks = TRUE)
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "African lion",
    subtitle = "Ethiopia’s GDP, % change on a year earlier",
    x = NULL, y = NULL
  ) +
  theme_economist_2017("print", base_size = 7)

economist_2017_chart(
  lion +
    labs(caption = "Source: IMF"),
  media = "print",
  footnote = "*Estimate"
)
```

### One trace with highlight

```{r salud, econ_height = 165}
doctors <- data.frame(
  country = c("Sweden", "Denmark", "Britain", "Portugal", "Luxembourg",
              "France", "Austria", "Spain", "Germany"),
  visits = c(2.9, 4.6, 5.0, 5.7, 6.3, 6.9, 6.9, 7.5, 8.2)
)
doctors$country <- factor(doctors$country, levels = doctors$country)
doctors$highlight <- doctors$country == "Spain"

salud <- ggplot(doctors, aes(country, visits, fill = highlight)) +
  geom_col(width = 0.6, show.legend = FALSE) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, colour = print_pal$baseline, linewidth = 0.3) +
  coord_flip() +
  scale_y_continuous(guide = guide_axis_economist_2017(), position = "right", expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.02))) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c(`FALSE` = pal_bar(1), `TRUE` = pal_bar(2)[2])) +
  labs(
    title = "Salud",
    subtitle = "Doctors’ consultations per person\nSelected countries, 2009",
    x = NULL, y = NULL
  ) +
  ## The guide sets the highlighted category's label in bold.
  scale_x_discrete(labels = bold_label("Spain")) +
  theme_economist_2017("print", horizontal = FALSE, base_size = 7)

economist_2017_chart(
  salud +
    labs(caption = "Source: OECD"),
  media = "print"
)
```

### Two traces with sub-categories

```{r autumn-fall, econ_height = 185}
forecasts <- data.frame(
  country = rep(c("Germany", "France", "Euro area", "Spain", "Italy"), each = 4),
  vintage = rep(rep(c("2011", "2012"), each = 2), 5),
  made_in = rep(c("June", "September"), 10),
  gdp = c(3.2, 2.7, 2.0, 1.3, 2.1, 1.7, 1.9, 1.4, 2.0, 1.6,
          1.7, 1.1, 0.8, 0.8, 1.6, 1.1, 1.0, 0.6, 1.3, 0.3)
)
forecasts$country <- factor(forecasts$country, levels = unique(forecasts$country))
forecasts$vintage <- factor(forecasts$vintage, levels = c("2012", "2011"))
forecasts$made_in <- factor(forecasts$made_in, levels = c("June", "September"))

## A rule above every group but the first.
autumn_rules <- data.frame(country = factor(levels(forecasts$country)[-1], levels = levels(forecasts$country)))

autumn <- ggplot(forecasts, aes(vintage, gdp, fill = made_in)) +
  geom_col(position = position_dodge(width = 0.7, reverse = TRUE), width = 0.7) +
  geom_vline(data = autumn_rules, aes(xintercept = 2.5), colour = grid_col, linewidth = 0.3) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, colour = print_pal$baseline, linewidth = 0.3) +
  coord_flip() +
  facet_grid(rows = vars(.data$country), scales = "free_y", space = "free", switch = "y") +
  scale_x_discrete(expand = expansion(add = 0.5)) +
  scale_y_continuous(
    guide = guide_axis_economist_2017(), position = "right", breaks = 0:3, expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.02))
  ) +
  scale_fill_economist_2017("print", type = "bar_side") +
  labs(
    title = "Autumn fall",
    subtitle = "GDP, % increase on previous year",
    x = NULL, y = NULL, fill = "Forecasts made in:"
  ) +
  theme_economist_2017("print", horizontal = FALSE, base_size = 7) +
  theme(
    strip.placement = "outside",
    strip.text.y.left = element_text(angle = 0, hjust = 0, vjust = 1),
    panel.spacing.y = unit(0, "pt")
  ) +
  guides(fill = guide_legend(title.position = "left"))

economist_2017_chart(
  autumn +
    labs(caption = "Source: IMF"),
  media = "print"
)
```

### Color overrides

> Where categories are chronological, use light-to-dark scale

```{r growth-asia, econ_height = 225}

asia$period <- factor(asia$period, levels = c("2015", "2016", "2016-20*"))

## Light to dark: the palette's two cyans, then the guide's navy.

growth <- ggplot(asia, aes(country, growth, fill = period)) +
  geom_col(position = position_dodge(width = 0.76, reverse = TRUE), width = 0.76) +

  scale_y_continuous(guide = guide_axis_economist_2017(), position = "right", limits = c(-2, 8),

  scale_fill_manual(values = chrono) +
  labs(
    title = "Growth in Asia",
    subtitle = "GDP forecasts, % change on a year earlier",
    x = NULL, y = NULL, fill = NULL
  ) +
  theme_economist_2017("print", horizontal = FALSE, base_size = 7)

economist_2017_chart(
  growth +
    labs(caption = "Source: OECD"),
  media = "print",
  footnote = "*Annual average"
)
```

> If categories form meaningful groups, use colour to reinforce that

```{r dont-fence, econ_height = 235}
segregation <- data.frame(
  group = rep(c("White British", "Other White", "Mixed", "Bangladeshi",
                "Pakistani", "Indian", "Chinese", "African", "Caribbean"), each = 4),
  area = rep(c("Inner London", "Outer London",
               "Metropolitan areas", "Other large cities"), 9),
  change = c(
    3.0, 1.7, 1.6, 0.4, -2.7, -0.7, -1.7, 0, -6.3, -8.3, -10.4, -9.3,
    -0.1, -11.8, -3.7, -3.1, -1.0, -4.6, -3.0, -5.3, 0, -1.5, -5.3, -5.2,
    -6.1, -11.5, -11.9, -10.2, 0.3, -3.8, -14.8, -19.9, 1.3, -4.8, -4.7, -7.1
  )
)
segregation$group <- factor(segregation$group, levels = rev(unique(segregation$group)))
segregation$area <- factor(segregation$area, levels = c(
  "Inner London", "Outer London", "Metropolitan areas", "Other large cities"
))

## Reds for the two London rows, blues for the two city rows.
grouped <- c(pal_bar(6)[5], pal_bar(6)[6], pal_bar(6)[1], pal_bar(6)[2])

fence <- ggplot(segregation, aes(group, change, fill = area)) +
  geom_col(position = position_dodge(width = 0.76, reverse = TRUE), width = 0.76) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, colour = econ_red, linewidth = 0.2) +
  coord_flip() +
  scale_y_continuous(guide = guide_axis_economist_2017(), position = "right", limits = c(-20, 5),
                     breaks = seq(-20, 5, 5), expand = expansion(0)) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = grouped) +
  labs(
    title = "Don’t fence me in",
    subtitle = "Britain, % change in segregation index*\n2001-11",
    x = NULL, y = NULL, fill = NULL
  ) +
  theme_economist_2017("print", horizontal = FALSE, base_size = 7) +
  ## The guide reads the key down its columns.
  guides(fill = guide_legend(nrow = 2, byrow = FALSE))

economist_2017_chart(
  fence +
    labs(caption = "Source: University\nof Manchester"),
  media = "print",
  footnote = "* % that needs to move to\ncreate an even distribution"
)
```

## Bar / column, stacked

Stacked bars use the `stacked` order. 

> For stacked bars with few categories or labelling issues, consider
> removing tick marks and labelling each segment value.

```{r fed-nuptials, econ_height = 149}
carriers <- data.frame(
  band = rep(c("All mobiles", "Smartphones"), each = 5),
  carrier = rep(c("AT&T", "T-Mobile", "Sprint Nextel", "Verizon", "Other"), 2),
  share = c(30.4, 10.0, 31.4, 11.1, 16.8, 44.1, 9.6, 30.5, 12.9, 8.0),
  ## Segment widths as drawn in the guide.
  width = c(26.5, 10.1, 31.5, 11.0, 20.9, 35.1, 12.2, 29.6, 14.8, 8.3)
)
carriers$carrier <- factor(carriers$carrier, levels = unique(carriers$carrier))
carriers$band <- factor(carriers$band, levels = c("Smartphones", "All mobiles"))
## Each bar is headed by its name, ranged left above it, in place of axis labels.
bands <- data.frame(band = levels(carriers$band), row = 1:2)

fed <- ggplot(carriers, aes(band, width, fill = carrier)) +
  ## reverse = TRUE so the bar reads in color order from the left.
  geom_col(width = 0.55, position = position_stack(reverse = TRUE)) +
  ## Segment values start at the segment's left edge.
  geom_text(
    aes(label = sprintf("%.1f", share)),
    position = position_stack(vjust = 0, reverse = TRUE),
    hjust = -0.12, colour = "white", fontface = "bold", size = 6.8 / ggplot2::.pt
  ) +
  geom_text(
    data = bands, aes(x = row + 0.29, y = 0, label = band), inherit.aes = FALSE,
    hjust = 0, vjust = 0, fontface = "bold", size = 6.5 / ggplot2::.pt, colour = print_pal$text
  ) +
  coord_flip(clip = "off") +
  scale_x_discrete(expand = expansion(add = c(0.3, 0.45))) +
  scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0, 100), expand = expansion(0)) +
  ## The key is ordered alphabetically, down its columns, not in bar order.
  scale_fill_economist_2017(
    "print", type = "stacked",
    breaks = c("AT&T", "Sprint Nextel", "T-Mobile", "Verizon", "Other")
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "The Fed says no to nuptials",
    subtitle = "Mobile operators' US market share\nJuly 2011, %",
    x = NULL, y = NULL, fill = NULL
  ) +
  theme_economist_2017("print", base_size = 7) +
  no_value_axis() +
  theme(axis.text.y = element_blank(), axis.ticks.y = element_blank()) +
  guides(fill = guide_legend(nrow = 2, byrow = FALSE))

economist_2017_chart(
  fed +
    labs(caption = "Source: comScore"),
  media = "print"
)
```

```{r no-winner, econ_height = 129}
## Drawn in the guide's own units, so the leader lines can be placed.
seats <- data.frame(
  party = c("ERC", "DiL", "EAJ-PNV", "Others", "Podemos", "PSOE", "Ciudadanos", "PP"),
  n = c(9, 8, 6, 5, 69, 90, 40, 123),
  ## Color order with swaps: red and mauve from bar, navy from stacked, grey for others.
  fill = c(pal_bar(6)[5], pal_stack(6)[3], pal_stack(6)[6], "#97AFBA", pal_stack(6)[2],
           pal_stack(6)[1], pal_bar(6)[6], pal_stack(6)[4])
)
seats$xmax <- cumsum(seats$n)
seats$xmin <- seats$xmax - seats$n
seats$mid <- (seats$xmin + seats$xmax) / 2
sx <- function(px) (px - 40) / 591 * 350
bar_top <- 226
bar_bottom <- 321

## Leader lines from the small segments to the names beneath the bar, as
## (x, y) corners of each path.
leaders <- list(
  ERC = list(x = c(seats$mid[1], seats$mid[1]), y = c(bar_bottom, 392)),
  DiL = list(x = c(seats$mid[2], seats$mid[2], sx(157), sx(157)), y = c(bar_bottom, 378, 378, 392)),
  `EAJ-PNV` = list(x = c(seats$mid[3], seats$mid[3], sx(256), sx(256)), y = c(bar_bottom, 363, 363, 392)),
  Others = list(x = c(seats$mid[4], seats$mid[4], sx(414), sx(414)), y = c(bar_bottom, 351, 351, 392)),
  Ciudadanos = list(x = c(seats$mid[7], seats$mid[7], sx(437)), y = c((bar_top + bar_bottom) / 2, 345, 345))
)
paths <- do.call(rbind, lapply(names(leaders), function(nm) {
  data.frame(party = nm, x = leaders[[nm]]$x, y = leaders[[nm]]$y)
}))
## Where each key square sits, and its name.
keys <- data.frame(
  party = c("ERC", "DiL", "EAJ-PNV", "Others", "Ciudadanos"),
  x = sx(c(43, 152, 251, 410, 437)),
  y = c(405, 405, 405, 405, 345)
)
keys$fill <- seats$fill[match(keys$party, seats$party)]
keys$label <- paste(keys$party, seats$n[match(keys$party, seats$party)])
dots <- data.frame(
  x = seats$mid[c(1, 2, 3, 4, 7)],
  y = c(rep(bar_bottom - 4, 4), (bar_top + bar_bottom) / 2)
)
axis_y <- 179
axis_breaks <- data.frame(x = c(0, 176, 350), label = c("0", "176 required for majority", "350"))

winner <- ggplot() +
  geom_rect(
    data = seats,
    aes(xmin = xmin, xmax = xmax, ymin = bar_top, ymax = bar_bottom, fill = fill),
    colour = print_bg, linewidth = 0.15
  ) +
  geom_path(data = paths, aes(x, y, group = party), colour = print_pal$text, linewidth = 0.2) +
  geom_point(data = dots, aes(x, y), size = 0.5) +
  geom_rect(data = keys, aes(xmin = x, xmax = x + 6, ymin = y - 10, ymax = y + 10, fill = fill)) +
  geom_text(
    data = keys, aes(x + 10, y, label = label), hjust = 0, size = 6.5 / ggplot2::.pt,
    colour = print_pal$text
  ) +
  ## Values inside the big segments: the name in bold, the seats beneath.
  geom_text(
    data = subset(seats, party %in% c("Podemos", "PSOE")),
    aes(mid, 260, label = party), colour = "white", fontface = "bold", size = 6.5 / ggplot2::.pt
  ) +
  geom_text(
    data = subset(seats, party %in% c("Podemos", "PSOE")),
    aes(mid, 292, label = n), colour = "white", size = 6.5 / ggplot2::.pt
  ) +
  geom_text(
    data = subset(seats, party == "PP"), aes(mid, 276, label = 'bold("PP")~"123"'), parse = TRUE,
    colour = "white", size = 6.5 / ggplot2::.pt
  ) +
  ## The value axis is drawn by hand: a tick at each end and at the majority,
  ## which is named where it falls.
  geom_segment(
    data = axis_breaks, aes(x = x, xend = x, y = 200, yend = 218), colour = print_pal$text,
    linewidth = 0.3, lineend = "butt"
  ) +
  geom_text(
    data = axis_breaks, aes(x, axis_y, label = label), size = 6.8 / ggplot2::.pt,
    colour = print_pal$text
  ) +
  scale_fill_identity() +
  scale_x_continuous(limits = c(0, 350), expand = expansion(0)) +
  scale_y_reverse(limits = c(425, 165), expand = expansion(0)) +
  coord_cartesian(clip = "off") +
  labs(
    title = "No one's a winner",
    subtitle = "Spanish general election 2015, Seats won",
    x = NULL, y = NULL
  ) +
  theme_economist_2017("print", base_size = 7) +
  theme(
    axis.text = element_blank(),
    axis.ticks = element_blank(),
    axis.line = element_blank(),
    panel.grid = element_blank(),
    legend.position = "none"
  )

economist_2017_chart(
  winner +
    labs(caption = "Sources: Ministry of the Interior; El País"),
  media = "print"
)
```

```{r looting, econ_height = 189}
## Drawn in the guide's own units; each bar has its own scale.
bars <- rbind(
  data.frame(
    row = 1, stream = c("Oil & gas", "Confiscation", "Tax", "Electricity"),
    value = c(20.1, 14.3, 12.0, 4.0), scale = 617 / 50.4, x0 = 33,
    fill = pal_stack(6)[1:4]
  ),
  data.frame(
    row = 2, stream = c("Oil & gas", "Confiscation", "Tax", "Electricity"),
    value = c(2.3, 3.8, 1.9, 0.4), scale = 61.2, x0 = 37, fill = pal_stack(6)[1:4]
  ),
  data.frame(
    row = 3, stream = c("Fighters' salary", "Military camps", "Social services", "Islamic police", "Treasury", "Media"),
    value = c(2.5, 1.15, 1.0, 0.6, 0.35, 0.2), scale = 61.2, x0 = 37,
    ## The spending bar's own colours, as printed.
    fill = c(swatch("red1"), "#EDA510", swatch("purple"), "#2EB3C6", swatch("lime"), "#23635E")
  )
)
bars$xmax <- unlist(lapply(split(bars, bars$row), function(d) d$x0 + cumsum(d$value) * d$scale))
bars$xmin <- bars$xmax - bars$value * bars$scale
bars$ymin <- c(258, 452, 592)[bars$row]
bars$ymax <- c(312, 497, 632)[bars$row]
bars$mid <- (bars$xmin + bars$xmax) / 2

## Panel headings: a bold lead-in, then the rest, under a red marker.
headings <- data.frame(
  y = c(188, 380, 560),
  label = c(
    'bold("Overall")~"Monthly revenue $79.8m"',
    'bold("Deir al-Zor governorate")~"Monthly revenue $8.7m"',
    'bold("Monthly spending")~"$5.8m"'
  )
)
markers <- data.frame(y = c(163, 353))
## The first bar's key runs along its heading; the third bar's names have leader lines.
keys <- data.frame(
  x = c(38, 221, 428, 521, 40, 170, 640, 640, 640, 640),
  y = c(237, 237, 237, 237, 655, 655, 571, 610, 646, 686),
  label = c("Oil & gas", "Confiscation", "Tax", "Electricity", "Fighters'\nsalary", "Military\ncamps",
            "Treasury", "Media", "Islamic police", "Social services"),
  fill = c(pal_stack(6)[1:4], bars$fill[bars$row == 3][c(1, 2, 5, 6, 4, 3)])
)
keys$left <- keys$x < 600
## Leader lines from the segments to the names on the right, as (x, y) corners.
lead <- list(
  Treasury = list(x = c(365, 365, 495), y = c(600, 571, 571)),
  Media = list(x = c(380, 525), y = c(612, 610)),
  Police = list(x = c(337, 337, 435), y = c(632, 646, 646)),
  Social = list(x = c(288, 288, 415), y = c(625, 686, 686))
)
lead_paths <- do.call(rbind, lapply(names(lead), function(nm) {
  data.frame(id = nm, x = lead[[nm]]$x, y = lead[[nm]]$y)
}))
## The middle bar's own 0--10 axis: labels above, rules through the bar.
ticks <- data.frame(x = 37 + 61.2 * seq(0, 10, 2), label = seq(0, 10, 2))
ticks$colour <- ifelse(ticks$x == 37, print_pal$text, grid_col)

looting <- ggplot() +
  geom_segment(
    data = ticks, aes(x = x, xend = x, y = 437, yend = 510, colour = colour), linewidth = 0.25
  ) +
  geom_text(data = ticks, aes(x, 422, label = label), size = 6.8 / ggplot2::.pt, colour = print_pal$text) +
  geom_rect(data = bars, aes(xmin = xmin, xmax = xmax, ymin = ymin, ymax = ymax, fill = fill)) +
  geom_text(
    data = subset(bars, row == 1), aes(mid, 285, label = c("20.1", "14.3", "12.0", "4")),
    colour = "white", fontface = "bold", size = 6.8 / ggplot2::.pt
  ) +
  geom_segment(
    data = markers, aes(x = 33, xend = 33 + 42, y = y, yend = y), colour = econ_red, linewidth = 0.4
  ) +
  geom_text(
    data = headings, aes(33, y, label = label), parse = TRUE, hjust = 0, size = 6.8 / ggplot2::.pt,
    colour = print_pal$text
  ) +
  geom_path(data = lead_paths, aes(x, y, group = id), colour = print_pal$text, linewidth = 0.2) +
  geom_point(data = data.frame(x = c(365, 380, 337, 288), y = c(600, 612, 632, 625)), aes(x, y), size = 0.5) +
  geom_rect(data = keys, aes(xmin = x, xmax = x + 10, ymin = y - 10, ymax = y + 10, fill = fill)) +
  geom_text(
    data = subset(keys, left), aes(x + 16, y + ifelse(y > 600, 16, 0), label = label), hjust = 0,
    lineheight = 1.1, size = 6.5 / ggplot2::.pt, colour = print_pal$text
  ) +
  geom_text(
    data = subset(keys, !left), aes(x - 9, y, label = label), hjust = 1, size = 6.5 / ggplot2::.pt,
    colour = print_pal$text
  ) +
  scale_fill_identity() +
  scale_colour_identity() +
  scale_x_continuous(limits = c(32, 652), expand = expansion(0)) +
  scale_y_reverse(limits = c(705, 150), expand = expansion(0)) +
  coord_cartesian(clip = "off") +
  labs(
    title = "Looting the Levant",
    subtitle = "Islamic State's finances*, January 2015, $m",
    x = NULL, y = NULL
  ) +
  theme_economist_2017("print", base_size = 7) +
  theme(
    axis.text = element_blank(),
    axis.ticks = element_blank(),
    axis.line = element_blank(),
    panel.grid = element_blank(),
    legend.position = "none"
  )

economist_2017_chart(
  looting +
    labs(caption = "Sources: IHS"),
  media = "print",
  footnote = "*Estimates"
)
```

```{r getting-sociable, econ_height = 178}
adspend <- data.frame(

  )
)

economist_2017_chart(

    labs(caption = "Source: ZenithOptimedia"),
  media = "print"
)
```

### Color overrides

> You may need to swap in other colours for charts with more than 4 categories
>
> Use grey for ‘other’ / ‘dont know’ etc

```{r movers-shakers, econ_height = 179}
## Origins in stack order; a bar skips origins it lacks.
origins <- c("Romania", "Poland", "Italy", "Portugal", "Germany", "Britain")
shares <- rbind(
  `EU-28` = c(20, 15, 9, 7.5, 5, 0),
  Switzerland = c(0, 0, 20.5, 21, 24, 0),
  Germany = c(5.5, 17.5, 18.5, 0, 0, 0),
  Spain = c(46.5, 0, 9.5, 6, 0, 8),
  France = c(0, 0, 7.5, 42, 0, 8),
  Italy = c(76, 7.5, 0, 0, 0, 0),
  Britain = c(5.5, 29.5, 0, 5.5, 0, 0)
)
migrants <- data.frame(
  destination = rep(rownames(shares), times = ncol(shares) + 1),
  origin = rep(c(origins, "Other"), each = nrow(shares)),
  pct = c(shares, 100 - rowSums(shares))
)
migrants$origin <- factor(migrants$origin, levels = c(origins, "Other"))
migrants$destination <- factor(migrants$destination, levels = rev(rownames(shares)))

## Blue, cyan, gold and teal from the stacked order, then red and navy, with grey for "other".
movers_cols <- c(pal_stack(6)[1:4], pal_bar(6)[5], pal_stack(6)[6], "#97AFBA")

movers <- ggplot(migrants, aes(destination, pct, fill = origin)) +
  geom_col(width = 0.75, position = position_stack(reverse = TRUE)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, colour = print_pal$text, linewidth = 0.2) +
  annotate("text", x = 7, y = 78, label = "Other", hjust = 0.5, size = 8 / ggplot2::.pt, colour = print_pal$text) +
  coord_flip() +
  scale_y_continuous(
    guide = guide_axis_economist_2017(), position = "right", limits = c(0, 100),
    breaks = seq(0, 100, 20), expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0))
  ) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = setNames(movers_cols, c(origins, "Other")), breaks = origins) +
  labs(
    title = "Movers and shakers",
    subtitle = "Intra-European* migrants living elsewhere\n2014, % of total by destination country",
    x = NULL, y = NULL, fill = NULL
  ) +
  theme_economist_2017("print", base_size = 7) +
  theme(panel.grid.major = element_blank()) +
  guides(fill = guide_legend(nrow = 2, byrow = TRUE))

economist_2017_chart(
  movers +
    labs(caption = "Source: European Commission"),
  media = "print",
  footnote = "*Including EFTA"
)
```


> If categories form meaningful groups, use colour to reinforce that

```{r trumps-troops, econ_height = 249}
answers <- c("Enthusiastic", "Satisfied", "Dissatisfied", "Upset", "Not sure")
## Rows top to bottom, with segment widths and number blocks.
troops <- data.frame(
  head = c("White men", "White women", "White men", "Non-white men", "White women", "Non-white men",
           "Non-white women", "Non-white women"),
  tail = c("no college", "no college", "college educated", "college educated", "college educated",
           "no college", "college educated", "no college"),
  share = c(22, 24, 16, 3, 17, 6, 4, 7)
)
troops$row <- rev(seq_len(nrow(troops)))
pct <- rbind(
  c(29, 24, 14, 31, 2), c(25, 19, 13, 40, 3), c(18, 17, 17, 47, 1), c(18, 12, 11, 51, 8),
  c(13, 15, 14, 57, 1), c(11, 12, 19, 52, 6), c(4, 9, 15, 70, 2), c(5, 7, 17, 67, 4)
)
bars <- data.frame(
  row = rep(troops$row, times = length(answers)),
  answer = factor(rep(answers, each = nrow(troops)), levels = answers),
  pct = c(pct)
)

## Positive answers take the blues, negative ones the reds, "not sure" grey.
troop_cols <- c(pal_stack(6)[1:2], pal_bar(6)[6], pal_bar(6)[5], "#97AFBA")
block_col <- "#7F98A4"
left <- -83

trump <- ggplot(bars, aes(row, pct, fill = answer)) +
  geom_col(width = 0.55, position = position_stack(reverse = TRUE)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, colour = print_pal$text, linewidth = 0.2) +
  ## Each row is named in two lines, the first bold.
  geom_text(
    data = troops, aes(row + 0.2, left, label = head), inherit.aes = FALSE, hjust = 0,
    fontface = "bold", size = 6.8 / ggplot2::.pt, colour = print_pal$text
  ) +
  geom_text(
    data = troops, aes(row - 0.2, left, label = tail), inherit.aes = FALSE, hjust = 0,
    size = 6.8 / ggplot2::.pt, colour = print_pal$text
  ) +
  ## Number blocks right of the 100% mark; the smallest figure sits beside its block.
  geom_point(data = troops, aes(row, 120, size = share), inherit.aes = FALSE, colour = block_col) +
  geom_text(
    data = subset(troops, share != 3), aes(row, 120, label = share), inherit.aes = FALSE,
    colour = "white", fontface = "bold", size = 6.8 / ggplot2::.pt
  ) +
  geom_text(
    data = subset(troops, share == 3), aes(row, 125, label = share), inherit.aes = FALSE, hjust = 0,
    colour = block_col, fontface = "bold", size = 6.8 / ggplot2::.pt
  ) +
  ## The heading of the number blocks: a text block pointing down at them.
  annotate("label_economist_2017", x = 9.6, y = 120, label = "% of total voters\n2012", pointer = "bottom",
    hjust = 0.82,
    padding = 2, fill = block_col, colour = "white", fontface = "bold", size = 6.8 / ggplot2::.pt
  ) +
  coord_flip(xlim = c(0.55, 8.45), clip = "off") +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = NULL) +
  scale_size_area(max_size = 7.9, guide = "none") +
  scale_y_continuous(
    guide = guide_axis_economist_2017(), position = "right", limits = c(left, 134),
    breaks = seq(0, 100, 20), expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0))
  ) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = troop_cols) +
  labs(
    title = "Trump's troops",
    subtitle = "How do you feel about Donald Trump as\nthe 2016 Republican nominee\nfor president?*",
    x = NULL, y = NULL, fill = NULL
  ) +
  theme_economist_2017("print", base_size = 7) +
  theme(panel.grid.major = element_blank()) +
  guides(fill = guide_legend(ncol = 2, byrow = TRUE))

economist_2017_chart(
  trump +
    labs(caption = "Sources: YouGov;\nCCES;\nThe Economist"),
  media = "print",
  footnote = "*5,773 registered voters surveyed\nJune 4th to July 9th 2016"
)
```

```{r penumbral, econ_height = 165}
## Quarterly (or finer) steps.
ink <- theme_economist_2017("print", base_size = 7)$text$colour
tick_col <- theme_economist_2017("print", base_size = 7)$axis.ticks$colour

## Year-boundary ticks are minor ticks drawn full length; the label's own tick is hidden.
span_axis <- guide_axis(
  minor.ticks = TRUE,
  theme = theme(
    axis.ticks.x.bottom = element_line(colour = "transparent"),
    axis.minor.ticks.x.bottom = element_line(colour = tick_col),
    axis.minor.ticks.length.x.bottom = unit(5, "pt")
  )
)

shadow <- data.frame(
  year = 2006 + 0.125 * (0:42),
  units = c(
    0.4, 0.39, 0.38, 0.39, 0.42, 0.43, 0.46, 0.5, 0.54, 0.55, 0.59, 0.65, 0.71, 0.79, 0.88, 0.98, 1.09, 1.14, 1.19,

  )

  ) +
  scale_x_continuous(
    limits = c(2006, 2012.05), expand = c(0, 0), guide = span_axis,

    labels = c("2006", "07", "08", "09", "10", "11")

economist_2017_chart(

  footnote = "*Foreclosed and delinquent\nhomes not yet on the market"
)
```

```{r line-order, econ_size = "three_column", econ_height = 300}
## Shapes per panel, one value per step.
line_shape <- list(
  A = c(
    3.62, 3.59, 3.52, 3.51, 3.48, 3.46, 3.44, 3.4, 3.34, 3.34, 3.27, 3.15, 3.09, 3.07, 3.06, 2.97,
    2.93, 2.89, 2.83, 2.8, 2.78, 2.73, 2.68, 2.68
  ),
  B = c(
    2.61, 2.66, 2.67, 2.7, 2.66, 2.63, 2.65, 2.65, 2.72, 2.78, 2.81, 2.82, 2.8, 2.75, 2.66, 2.62,
    2.48, 2.39, 2.32, 2.23, 2.13, 2.05, 1.98, 1.97
  ),
  C = c(
    2.11, 2.11, 2.08, 1.97, 1.95, 1.96, 1.92, 1.84, 1.77, 1.68, 1.65, 1.62, 1.59, 1.49, 1.46, 1.41,
    1.37, 1.35, 1.31, 1.28, 1.25, 1.25, 1.23, 1.23
  ),
  D = c(
    0.22, 0.24, 0.42, 0.51, 0.61, 0.65, 0.73, 0.93, 1.07, 1.23, 1.63, 1.48, 1.5, 1.69, 1.77, 1.92,
    1.89, 1.72, 1.66, 1.64, 1.62, 1.6, 1.57, 1.48
  ),
  E = c(
    -0.18, -0.14, -0.1, -0.09, -0.1, -0.11, -0.1, -0.09, -0.06, -0.04, 0, 0.05, 0.09, 0.12, 0.16,
    0.23, 0.27, 0.31, 0.38, 0.46, 0.51, 0.54, 0.56, 0.56
  ),
  F = c(
    2.06, 1.98, 1.98, 1.97, 1.96, 1.98, 2.01, 2.01, 2.01, 2.04, 2.03, 2.02, 2.01, 2.01, 2.02, 2.03,
    2.02, 1.96, 1.9, 1.86, 1.85, 1.85, 1.86, 1.85
  )
)
## Which shape each series (in colour order) takes in the 1- to 6-line panels.
line_panels <- list(
  c("B"),
  c("A", "B"),
  c("A", "B", "D"),
  c("A", "C", "B", "D"),
  c("A", "B", "F", "E", "D"),
  c("A", "B", "F", "D", "C", "E")
)
line_demo <- do.call(rbind, lapply(seq_along(line_panels), function(n) {
  do.call(rbind, lapply(seq_along(line_panels[[n]]), function(k) {
    data.frame(
      panel = paste(n, if (n == 1) "line" else "lines"),
      series = factor(k, levels = 1:6),
      x = 1:24,
      y = line_shape[[line_panels[[n]][k]]]
    )
  }))
}))
line_demo$panel <- factor(line_demo$panel, levels = unique(line_demo$panel))

ggplot(line_demo, aes(x, y, colour = series)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1.4, show.legend = FALSE) +
  facet_wrap(~panel, nrow = 2) +
  scale_x_continuous(limits = c(-0.8, 25.6), expand = c(0, 0)) +
  scale_y_continuous(limits = c(-0.76, 4.69), breaks = 0:4, expand = c(0, 0)) +
  scale_colour_economist_2017("print", type = "line_side") +
  labs(title = "Standard colour order", x = NULL, y = NULL) +
  theme_economist_2017("print", base_size = 7) +
  theme(
    axis.text = element_blank(),
    axis.ticks = element_blank(),
    axis.line = element_blank()
  )
```

## Lines, stacked

Stacked areas use the `stacked` order, labeled in place where a band is wide enough.

```{r foreign-hoards, econ_height = 154}
china <- c(
  0.26, 0.36, 0.56, 0.77, 1.02, 1.49, 1.91, 2.3, 2.64, 2.96
)
other <- c(
  0.77, 0.98, 1.23, 1.51, 2.03, 2.86, 3.02, 3.19, 3.54, 3.77
)
reserves <- data.frame(
  year = rep(2002:2011, 2),
  trn = c(china, other),
  region = factor(rep(c("China", "Other developing countries"), each = 10),
                  levels = c("China", "Other developing countries"))
)

## A white rule along the top of every band but the last.
```

## Thermometer

A range between values per category, with short vertical terminals.  

### Standard color order

> Ilex will plot up to 6 colours but any more than 4 categories is probably
> too many and you should have a rethink

```{r thermometer-data}
fields <- c("Mathematics", "Economics", "Computer Science", "Business", "Biology",
            "Philosophy", "English", "Psychology", "History", "Communication")
series_names <- c("one", "two", "three", "four", "five", "six")

## One table of values per series count.
thermo_values <- list(
  `2` = list(
    c(31, 40, 72, 36, 39, 43, 35, 15, 20, 33),
    c(416, 398, 382, 316, 308, 275, 290, 239, 283, 251)
  ),
  `3` = list(
    c(31, 40, 72, 36, 39, 43, 35, 15, 20, 33),
    c(418, 398, 382, 316, 308, 275, 290, 239, 283, 251),
    c(395, 316, 292, 266, 257, 215, 201, 199, 197, 187)
  ),
  `4` = list(
    c(280, 249, 117, 191, 84, 148, 80, 60, 134, 121),
    c(402, 316, 292, 266, 257, 214, 201, 199, 197, 187),
    c(339, 397, 381, 315, 307, 275, 290, 239, 283, 250),
    c(31, 40, 72, 36, 39, 43, 35, 15, 20, 33)
  ),
  `6` = list(
    c(222, 191, 172, 133, 16, 180, 152, 104, 233, 109),
    c(405, 398, 382, 316, 308, 276, 290, 238, 284, 251),
    c(280, 249, 117, 192, 84, 147, 80, 60, 135, 121),
    c(31, 40, 72, 37, 39, 43, 35, 15, 21, 34),
    c(335, 294, 134, 236, 129, 196, 52, 199, 260, 156),
    c(375, 317, 292, 266, 257, 214, 201, 199, 197, 187)
  ),
  dot = list(
    c(31, 41, 72, 37, 39, 43, 35, 15, 21, 34),
    c(419, 398, 382, 280, 308, 276, 290, 239, 284, 251),
    c(396, 317, 364, 263, 257, 215, 201, 222, 197, 187)
  )
)

thermo_data <- function(key) {
  values <- thermo_values[[key]]
  do.call(rbind, lapply(seq_along(values), function(k) {
    data.frame(
      field = factor(fields, levels = rev(fields)),
      series = factor(series_names[k], levels = series_names),
      value = values[[k]]
    )
  }))
}

## The connecting rule runs from the zero axis to the highest series.
thermo_plot <- function(n, terminals = c("rule", "dot")) {
  terminals <- match.arg(terminals)
  d <- thermo_data(if (terminals == "dot") "dot" else as.character(n))
  spans <- aggregate(value ~ field, d, max)

  ## The rule is the grid's own blue, a step darker; darker again under dots.
  p <- ggplot(d, aes(y = .data$field)) +
    geom_segment(data = spans, aes(x = 0, xend = .data$value, y = .data$field, yend = .data$field),
                 colour = if (terminals == "rule") "#92A9B4" else swatch("grey box"), linewidth = 0.47)
  p <- p + if (terminals == "rule") {
    ## Vertical rules, the default terminal.
    geom_linerange(aes(x = .data$value, ymin = as.numeric(.data$field) - 0.41,
                       ymax = as.numeric(.data$field) + 0.41, colour = .data$series),
                   linewidth = 1, key_glyph = "vline")
  } else {
    geom_point(aes(x = .data$value, colour = .data$series), size = 1.6)
  }

  ## "Horrible" sits on the axis-number row, left of the category labels.
  label_gp <- gpar(fontsize = 7, fontface = "bold")
  p +
    annotation_custom(textGrob(
      "\u201cHorrible\u201d", gp = label_gp, hjust = 0, vjust = 0,
      x = unit(0, "npc") - grobWidth(textGrob("Computer Science", gp = gpar(fontsize = 7))) + unit(1.5, "pt"),
      y = unit(1, "npc") + unit(2, "pt")
    )) +
    coord_cartesian(clip = "off") +
    scale_x_continuous(position = "top", limits = c(0, 425), breaks = seq(0, 400, 100),
                       expand = expansion(0)) +
    scale_colour_economist_2017("print", type = "dot") +
    labs(
      title = "The horrible science",
      subtitle = paste0("Use of specific \u201cadjective\u201d per million\n",
                        "words in student reviews on\n",
                        "RateMyProfessors.com*"),
      x = NULL, y = NULL, colour = NULL
    ) +
    theme_economist_2017("print", horizontal = FALSE, base_size = 7) +
    theme(axis.line.y = element_line(colour = "black", linewidth = 0.25))
}
```

## Scatter plot

### Chart elements

Standard dots are 4px at 50% opacity:

> use where general trend is more important than individual point

Highlight dots are 100% opaque:

> use to label outliers / important data points

Category dots have a 0.3px stroke and 50% fill. Trend lines are 1px, dashed 3px/1px.

```{r scatter-elements, econ_size = "one_column", econ_height = 410}
## The specimen is laid out in points from its top left.
spec_x <- function(px) (px - 30) * 0.2566
spec_y <- function(py) 410 - (py - 15) * 0.2566
blue <- pal_dot(6)[4]
red <- pal_dot(6)[2]
gold <- pal_dot(6)[3]
cyan <- pal_dot(6)[1]

## Dot specimens: three overlapping dots per row. Diameters are the guide's, in points.
dots <- data.frame(
  x = spec_x(rep(c(66, 102, 139), 6)),
  y = spec_y(rep(c(289, 665, 766, 1061, 1168, 1275), each = 3)),
  size = c(rep(72, 3 * 3), rep(c(36, 52, 76), 3)) * 0.2566 / 0.75 / ggplot2::.pt,
  colour = rep(c(cyan, blue, red, blue, red, gold), each = 3),
  kind = rep(c("standard", "highlight", "highlight", "category", "category", "category"), each = 3)
)
standard <- dots$kind == "standard"
highlight <- dots$kind == "highlight"
category <- dots$kind == "category"

notes <- data.frame(
  x = spec_x(219),
  y = spec_y(c(286, 337, 392, 445, 489, 531, 663, 714, 768, 822, 865,
               1055, 1105, 1160, 1214, 1257, 1483, 1533, 1588)),
  label = c("Standard dot", "4px width", "50% opacity",
            "use where general trend", "is more important than", "individual point",
            "highlight dot", "4px width", "100% opacity",
            "use to label outliers /", "important data points",
            "Category dot", "0.3px stroke", "50% opacity fill",
            "use for bubble charts", "to differential colours",
            "trend lines", "1px stroke", "dashed 3px, 1px"),
  face = c("bold", "plain", "plain", rep("italic", 3), "bold", "plain", "plain", rep("italic", 2),
           "bold", "plain", "plain", rep("italic", 2), "bold", "plain", "plain")
)

ggplot() +
  ## Standard dots, 50% opacity, so overlaps darken.
  geom_point(data = dots[standard, ], aes(x, y, size = size), colour = "transparent", fill = alpha(cyan, 0.5),
             shape = 21) +
  ## Highlight dots, 100% opacity with a hairline white edge to separate overlaps.
  geom_point(data = dots[highlight, ], aes(x, y, size = size, fill = colour), colour = "white",
             shape = 21, stroke = 0.2) +
  ## Category dots, 50% fill with a 0.3px stroke in the full colour.
  geom_point(data = dots[category, ], aes(x, y, size = size, colour = colour), shape = 21,
             fill = NA, stroke = 0.2) +
  geom_point(data = dots[category, ], aes(x, y, size = size, fill = alpha(colour, 0.5)),
             colour = "transparent", shape = 21) +
  geom_segment(aes(x = spec_x(58), xend = spec_x(193), y = spec_y(1485), yend = spec_y(1485)),
               colour = red, linewidth = 0.3, linetype = "31") +
  geom_text(data = notes, aes(x, y, label = label, fontface = face), hjust = 0, size = 3) +
  annotate("text", x = 0, y = spec_y(42), label = "Chart elements", hjust = 0, fontface = "bold", size = 4.9) +
  scale_size_identity() +
  scale_fill_identity() +
  scale_colour_identity() +
  scale_x_continuous(limits = c(0, 160), expand = c(0, 0)) +
  scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0, 410), expand = c(0, 0)) +
  coord_fixed(clip = "off") +
  theme_void() +
  theme(plot.background = element_rect(fill = "white", colour = NA),
        plot.margin = margin(0, 0, 0, 0))
```

### Standard scatter

```{r divergent, econ_height = 195}
set.seed(2017)
## The 1990-2007 cloud is tight and steep; the 2012-16 cloud is wide and flat.
## Five 1990-2007 outliers sit out to the right.
metro_old <- data.frame(employment = rnorm(240, 1.6, 1.1))
metro_old$house_prices <- 1.3 + 2.2 * metro_old$employment + rnorm(240, 0, 1.8)
metro_old <- rbind(metro_old, data.frame(employment = c(4.4, 4.8, 5.1, 5.9, 8.2),
                                         house_prices = c(2.8, 8.2, 7.9, 7.6, 6.6)))
metro_new <- data.frame(employment = rnorm(210, 2.1, 1.6))
metro_new$house_prices <- 3.5 + 0.67 * metro_new$employment + rnorm(210, 0, 3.9)

periods <- c("Q1 1990 - Q1 2007", "Q1 2012 - Q1 2016")
metro <- rbind(
  cbind(period = periods[2], metro_new),
  cbind(period = periods[1], metro_old)
)
metro$period <- factor(metro$period, levels = periods)

## Trend lines run over the span the guide draws them.
trends <- data.frame(
  period = factor(periods, levels = periods),
  x = c(-1.5, -0.7), xend = c(5.8, 8.2),
  y = c(-2, 3), yend = c(14.2, 9)
)

divergent <- ggplot(metro, aes(employment, house_prices, colour = period)) +
  geom_point(size = 1.4, alpha = 0.5) +
  geom_segment(data = trends, aes(x = x, xend = xend, y = y, yend = yend), linewidth = 0.5) +
  geom_segment(data = trends, aes(x = x, xend = xend, y = y, yend = yend), colour = "black",
               linewidth = 0.3, linetype = "31") +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, colour = econ_red, linewidth = 0.2) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, colour = econ_red, linewidth = 0.2) +
  coord_cartesian(xlim = c(-2.4, 8.8), ylim = c(-5, 20), expand = FALSE) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(-2, 8, 2)) +
  scale_y_continuous(guide = guide_axis_economist_2017(), position = "right", breaks = seq(-5, 20, 5)) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c("Q1 1990 - Q1 2007" = pal_dot(2)[2], "Q1 2012 - Q1 2016" = pal_dot(1))) +
  guides(colour = guide_legend(ncol = 1, override.aes = list(size = 2.2, alpha = 1))) +
  labs(
    title = "Divergent",
    subtitle = "United States, housing and employment\nMetro areas*, average annual change, %",
    x = "Employment", y = "House prices", colour = NULL
  ) +
  theme_economist_2017("print", base_size = 7) +
  theme(panel.grid.major.x = element_line(colour = grid_col), axis.line.x = element_blank(),
        axis.ticks.x = element_blank())

economist_2017_chart(
  divergent +
    labs(caption = "Sources: Freddie Mac;\nUS Bureau of Labour Statistics"),
  media = "print",
  footnote = "*At least\n100,000 population"
)
```

> sub title should summarise chart, save specific units for axis labels

> Same weight/colour for x and y ticks use black for zero baseline only

```{r disinfectant, econ_height = 166}
set.seed(11)
## A diffuse cloud of countries, plus a denser band of more open, less corrupt ones.
corruption <- data.frame(open = c(runif(55, 19, 63), runif(24, 60, 92)))
corruption$score <- c(
  pmin(55, pmax(5, 0.55 * (corruption$open[1:55] - 19) + 10 + rnorm(55, 0, 13))),
  runif(24, 33, 70)
)
named <- data.frame(
  country = c("Britain", "Denmark", "India", "Colombia", "US", "Sweden", "Mexico", "Singapore"),
  open = c(77.5, 91.7, 37.8, 37, 73.8, 86.8, 34.9, 83.7),
  score = c(96.5, 82.5, 67.4, 66, 69.6, 65.6, 53, 34.4),
  ## Where each label sits, relative to its dot, in data units.
  lx = c(76, 84.5, 42.8, 34.1, 70.9, 95.2, 19.6, 83.7),
  ly = c(91, 91, 75.4, 67.4, 70.2, 50, 52.6, 26.7),
  hjust = c(1, 0, 0.5, 1, 1, 0.5, 1, 0.5)
)
## Leader lines for the two labels that sit away from their dots.
leaders <- data.frame(x = c(20.5, 86.8, 92.6), xend = c(34.9, 92.6, 92.6),
                      y = c(53, 65.6, 65.6), yend = c(53, 65.6, 55))

disinfectant <- ggplot(corruption, aes(open, score)) +
  geom_point(colour = pal_dot(1), size = 1.4) +
  geom_segment(data = leaders, aes(x = x, xend = xend, y = y, yend = yend), colour = pal_dot(2)[2],
               linewidth = 0.2) +
  geom_point(data = named, colour = pal_dot(2)[2], size = 1.4) +
  geom_text(data = named, aes(x = lx, y = ly, label = country, hjust = hjust), size = 2.3, colour = "#5B6770") +
  scale_y_continuous(guide = guide_axis_economist_2017(), position = "right", limits = c(0, 100),
                     breaks = seq(0, 100, 20), expand = c(0, 0)) +

  labs(
    title = "The best disinfectant",
    subtitle = "Corruption and open data",
    x = "Corruption-perceptions index score, 2014\n100=least corrupt",
    y = "Open-data index score,\nlatest, 100=most open"
  ) +
  theme_economist_2017("print", base_size = 7) +
  theme(axis.title.x = element_text(hjust = 0.5), panel.grid.major.x = element_line(colour = grid_col),
        axis.line.x = element_blank(), axis.ticks.x = element_blank())

economist_2017_chart(
  disinfectant +
    labs(caption = "Sources: Transparency International;\nOpen Knowledge Foundation"),
```

### Bubble chart

Category dots have a 50% fill and a thin stroke, and are sized by a second variable.

```{r vitality, econ_size = "two_column", econ_height = 275}
set.seed(4)
regions <- c("Northeast", "Midwest", "West", "South")
## Per region: number of counties, health score mean and spread, swing at the mean health, and
## how large the counties are (log-mean of voting-eligible population).
region_spec <- data.frame(
  region = regions, n = c(150, 700, 70, 450),
  health_mean = c(42, 37.5, 50, 47), health_sd = c(6, 5, 8, 9),
  swing_mean = c(12, 15, -2, 5), swing_sd = c(7, 9, 11, 8), size_mean = c(1.2, 0.2, 1.6, 0.8)
)
counties <- do.call(rbind, lapply(seq_len(nrow(region_spec)), function(i) {
  r <- region_spec[i, ]
  health <- pmin(66, pmax(22, rnorm(r$n, r$health_mean, r$health_sd)))
  data.frame(
    region = r$region,
    health = health,
    swing = r$swing_mean - 1 * (health - r$health_mean) + rnorm(r$n, 0, r$swing_sd),
    pop = rlnorm(r$n, r$size_mean, 0.75)
  )
}))
## Drawn from the southern cloud up, so the Midwest and Northeast lie on top.
counties$region <- factor(counties$region, levels = c("South", "West", "Midwest", "Northeast"))
counties <- counties[order(counties$region), ]
counties$region <- factor(counties$region, levels = regions)

region_cols <- c(Northeast = pal_dot(6)[4], Midwest = pal_dot(6)[2], West = pal_dot(6)[3], South = pal_dot(6)[1])

## Arrows along the swing axis and at either end of the health axis; offsets in points.
note_col <- "#7C8F9B"
note_gp <- gpar(fontsize = 5.5, col = note_col)
arrow_note <- function(label, y, up) {
  grobTree(
    textGrob(label, x = unit(0, "npc") + unit(5, "pt"), y = unit(y, "npc"), rot = 90, gp = note_gp),
    polygonGrob(
      x = unit(0, "npc") + unit(5, "pt") + unit(c(-2.2, 2.2, 0), "pt"),
      y = unit(if (up) 0.985 else 0.015, "npc") + unit(if (up) c(0, 0, 4.4) else c(4.4, 4.4, 0), "pt") -
        unit(if (up) 4.4 else 2.2, "pt"),
      gp = gpar(fill = note_col, col = NA)
    )
  )
}
health_note <- function(label, left) {
  tip <- if (left) 0 else 1
  grobTree(
    textGrob(label, x = unit(tip, "npc") + unit(if (left) 7 else -7, "pt"), y = unit(0, "npc") - unit(14, "pt"),
             hjust = if (left) 0 else 1, gp = note_gp),
    polygonGrob(
      x = unit(tip, "npc") + unit(if (left) c(0, 4.4, 4.4) else c(0, -4.4, -4.4), "pt"),
      y = unit(0, "npc") + unit(c(-14, -11.8, -16.2), "pt"),
      gp = gpar(fill = note_col, col = NA)
    )
  )
}

## The key, drawn inside the panel at the top right: regions, then dot size.
vitality_key <- function(show_regions = TRUE) {
  region_key <- if (show_regions) {
    list(
      annotate("text", x = 61.1, y = 43.6, label = "Region", hjust = 0, fontface = "bold", size = 2.5),
      annotate("point", x = 61.1, y = c(38, 32.9, 27.4, 22.7), shape = 21, size = 3, stroke = 0.3,
               colour = region_cols[c(1, 2, 3, 4)], fill = alpha(region_cols[c(1, 2, 3, 4)], 0.5)),
      annotate("text", x = 62.4, y = c(38, 32.9, 27.4, 22.7), label = regions, hjust = 0, size = 2.5)
    )
  }
  c(region_key, list(
    annotate("point", x = 62.8, y = c(13, 9.6), shape = 1, size = c(6.6, 1.9), stroke = 0.3),
    annotate("text", x = 64.4, y = c(14.5, 10.2, 5.6), label = c("Voting", "eligible", "population"),
             hjust = 0, size = 2.5)
  ))
}

vitality_frame <- list(
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, colour = econ_red, linewidth = 0.2),
  scale_size_area(max_size = 6.6, guide = "none"),
  scale_y_continuous(guide = guide_axis_economist_2017(), position = "right", limits = c(-50.5, 50),
                     breaks = seq(-50, 50, 25), expand = c(0, 0)),
  scale_x_continuous(limits = c(20, 73), breaks = seq(20, 70, 10), expand = c(0, 0)),
  annotation_custom(arrow_note("MORE REPUBLICAN", 0.75, TRUE)),
  annotation_custom(arrow_note("LESS REPUBLICAN", 0.25, FALSE)),
  annotation_custom(health_note("WORSE HEALTH", TRUE)),
  annotation_custom(health_note("BETTER HEALTH", FALSE)),
  coord_cartesian(clip = "off"),
  theme_economist_2017("print", base_size = 7),
  theme(axis.title.x = element_text(hjust = 0.5), panel.grid.major.x = element_line(colour = grid_col),
        axis.line.x = element_blank(), axis.ticks.x = element_blank())
)

vitality <- ggplot(counties, aes(health, swing)) +
  geom_point(aes(fill = region, size = pop), shape = 21, alpha = 0.5, colour = "transparent") +
  geom_point(aes(colour = region, size = pop), shape = 21, fill = NA, alpha = 0.8, stroke = 0.3) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = region_cols, guide = "none") +
  scale_colour_manual(values = region_cols, guide = "none") +
  vitality_key() +
  vitality_frame +
  labs(
    title = "Vitality and the vote",
    subtitle = "United States, health metrics against swing to Donald Trump\nBy county",
    x = "Index of county health metrics*",
    y = "Change in Republican margin\nover Democrats, 2012-16, % points"
  )

economist_2017_chart(
  vitality +
    labs(caption = paste0("Sources: Atlas of US Presidential Elections; Census Bureau;\n",
                          "IPUMS, University of Minnesota; Institute for Health Metrics\n",
                          "and Evaluation; The Economist")),
  media = "print",
  footnote = "*Weighted index of obesity, diabetes,\nheavy drinking, physical exercise and\nlife expectancy, 2010-12"
)
```

## Tables

Tables cannot be made directly in `ggplot`, but are also replicated here, since some embed plots. The example tables here are created with `gt`.

```{r tables-setup}
## Fira Sans Condensed is loaded from Google Fonts, so tables use it whether or not it is installed.
econ_table_font <- list(gt::google_font("Fira Sans Condensed"), "Roboto Condensed", "Arial Narrow", "sans-serif")
rule_heavy <- gt::cell_borders(sides = "bottom", color = print_pal$text, weight = "0.5pt")
rule_light <- gt::cell_borders(sides = "bottom", color = swatch("black 50"), weight = "0.3pt")
stripe <- gt::cell_fill(color = swatch("highlight"))
detail <- function(x) sprintf('<span style="color:%s">%s</span>', print_pal$source, x)
medium <- function(x) sprintf('<span style="font-weight:500">%s</span>', x)

## The red tab, the title (9.5pt bold) and the subtitle (8pt), as on a chart.
econ_heading <- function(title, subtitle = NULL) {
  gt::html(paste0(
    sprintf('<div style="width:15pt;height:5pt;background:%s;margin:0 0 4pt 0"></div>', print_pal$accent),
    sprintf('<div style="font-weight:700;font-size:9.5pt;line-height:11pt">%s</div>', title),
    if (!is.null(subtitle)) sprintf('<div style="font-size:8pt;line-height:9.5pt;font-weight:400">%s</div>', subtitle)
  ))
}

## The source line (6.5pt, 75% black) with any footnotes ranged right.
econ_source <- function(source, footnote = "") {
  gt::html(sprintf(
    paste0(
      '<div style="display:flex;justify-content:space-between;align-items:flex-end;gap:6pt">',
      '<span>%s</span><span style="text-align:right">%s</span></div>'
    ),
    source, footnote
  ))
}

## Everything the tables share: the print background, the type, the rules
## and the padding, at the guide's width in points.
econ_table <- function(data, id, width = 160) {
  data |>
    gt::tab_options(
      table.width = sprintf("%gpt", width),
      table.background.color = print_pal$ground,
      table.font.size = "7.5pt",
      table.font.color = print_pal$text,
      table.font.weight = "300",
      table.border.top.style = "none",
      table.border.bottom.style = "none",
      table.margin.left = "0",
      heading.align = "left",
      heading.border.bottom.style = "none",
      heading.padding = "0",
      heading.padding.horizontal = "6pt",
      column_labels.font.weight = "500",
      column_labels.vlines.style = "none",
      column_labels.border.top.style = "none",
      column_labels.border.bottom.style = "solid",
      column_labels.border.bottom.width = "0.5pt",
      column_labels.border.bottom.color = print_pal$text,
      column_labels.padding = "2pt",
      column_labels.padding.horizontal = "3pt",
      row_group.font.weight = "500",
      row_group.border.top.style = "none",
      row_group.border.bottom.style = "solid",
      row_group.border.bottom.width = "0.5pt",
      row_group.border.bottom.color = print_pal$text,
      row_group.padding = "2pt",
      row_group.padding.horizontal = "3pt",
      table_body.border.top.style = "none",
      table_body.border.bottom.style = "none",
      table_body.hlines.style = "none",
      data_row.padding = "2pt",
      data_row.padding.horizontal = "3pt",
      source_notes.font.size = "6.5pt",
      source_notes.padding = "3pt",
      source_notes.padding.horizontal = "6pt",
      source_notes.border.bottom.style = "none",
      container.padding.x = "0",
      container.padding.y = "0"
    ) |>
    gt::opt_table_font(font = econ_table_font) |>
    gt::tab_style(gt::cell_text(color = print_pal$source), gt::cells_source_notes()) |>
    gt::opt_css(gsub("ID", id, "
      #ID .gt_table { line-height: 9pt; margin: 0 !important; }
      #ID .gt_heading { padding: 0 3pt 6pt 3pt !important; }
      #ID .gt_title, #ID .gt_subtitle { padding: 0 !important; }
      #ID .gt_col_heading { vertical-align: bottom; line-height: 9pt; }
      #ID .gt_row { vertical-align: top; line-height: 9pt; }
      #ID .nowrap { white-space: nowrap; }
    ", fixed = TRUE))
}
```

### Standard table

> Use 75k text to differentiate explanatory text

> Use alternating row colours to help with reading

```{r greatest-hits}
## "Greatest hits": each company's name over its description in 75% black,
## with every second row filled.
startups <- data.frame(
  company = c("Airbnb", "Dropbox", "Stripe", "Zenefits", "Instacart", "Docker"),
  about = c(
    "Rents out places<br>to stay for local hosts", "File-sharing and<br>storage in the cloud",
    "Software for selling<br>from within apps", "Online HR and<br>payroll services",
    "Grocery collection<br>and delivery service", "Platform to manage<br>distribution of software"
  ),
  value = c(25.5, 10, 5, 4.5, 2, 1.1),
  joined = c(2009, 2007, 2010, 2013, 2012, 2010)
)
startups$company <- paste0(medium(startups$company), "<br>", detail(startups$about))
startups$about <- NULL

gt::gt(startups, id = "greatest-hits") |>
  gt::fmt_markdown(company) |>
  gt::fmt_currency(value, decimals = 1) |>
  gt::cols_label(company = "Company", value = gt::html("Value*<br>$bn"), joined = gt::html("Date of<br>joining")) |>
  gt::cols_align("left") |>
  gt::cols_width(company ~ gt::pct(52), value ~ gt::pct(24), joined ~ gt::pct(24)) |>
  gt::tab_header(econ_heading("Greatest hits", "Largest Y Combinator-funded startups")) |>
  gt::tab_source_note(econ_source("Sources: CB Insights;<br>CrunchBase", "*Latest funding round")) |>
  econ_table("greatest-hits", width = 160) |>
  gt::tab_style(stripe, gt::cells_body(rows = c(2, 4, 6))) |>

```
