### Table with integrated charts

> Where table data will benefit from visualising, use small labelled bar
> charts etc.

```{r what-to-expect}
## A table with small inline SVG charts in its cells.
svg <- function(width, height, body) {
  sprintf(
    '<svg width="%gpt" height="%gpt" viewBox="0 0 %g %g" style="display:block">%s</svg>',
    width, height, width, height, paste(body, collapse = "")
  )
}
bar <- function(value, max, colour, width = 55, height = 3.5) {
  length <- pmax(width * value / max, 0.8)
  svg(width, height, sprintf('<rect width="%g" height="%g" fill="%s"/>', length, height, colour))
}
doughnut <- function(pct, label) {
  r <- 7.5
  paste0(
    '<div style="position:relative;width:22pt;height:22pt;margin:auto">',
    svg(22, 22, c(
      sprintf('<circle cx="11" cy="11" r="%g" fill="none" stroke="%s" stroke-width="3.5"/>', r, swatch("highlight")),
      sprintf(
        paste0(
          '<circle cx="11" cy="11" r="%g" fill="none" stroke="%s" stroke-width="3.5" pathLength="100" ',
          'stroke-dasharray="%g 100" transform="rotate(-90 11 11)"/>'
        ),
        r, swatch("navy"), pct
      )
    )),
    sprintf(
      paste0(
        '<span style="position:absolute;inset:0;display:flex;align-items:center;justify-content:center;',
        'font-weight:500;color:%s">%s</span>'
      ),
      swatch("navy"), label
    ),
    "</div>"
  )
}
dashes <- function(n) {
  if (n == 0) return("")
  svg(n * 6, 4, sprintf('<rect x="%g" y="1" width="5" height="2.2" fill="%s"/>', (seq_len(n) - 1) * 6, swatch("red1")))
}
dots <- function(n, per_row = 10) {
  i <- seq_len(n) - 1
  svg(per_row * 3.6, ceiling(n / per_row) * 3.6, sprintf(
    '<circle cx="%g" cy="%g" r="1.35" fill="%s"/>',
    1.8 + (i %% per_row) * 3.6, 1.8 + (i %/% per_row) * 3.6, swatch("navy")
  ))
}
colour <- function(x, col, weight = 400) sprintf('<span style="color:%s;font-weight:%d">%s</span>', col, weight, x)
dagger <- function(x, mark) paste0(x, ifelse(mark == "", "", paste0("<sup>", mark, "</sup>")))

asylum <- data.frame(
  country = c("Germany", "Sweden", "Hungary", "Britain", "United<br>States", "Australia"),
  applications = c(173070, 75090, 41370, 31260, 121160, 8960),
  decisions = c(97415, 40015, 5445, 26055, 71765, 13198),
  decisions_mark = c("", "", "", "", "†", "†"),
  accepted = c(42, 77, 9, 39, 30, 19),
  accepted_mark = c("", "", "", "", "†", "†"),
  wait = c("3 months", "Immediately", "9 months", "12 months", "6 months", ""),
  wait_months = c(3, 0, 9, 12, 6, 0),
  wait_note = c(
    "", "Without restrictions", "Working only in a<br>reception centre",
    "Only jobs where gov’t sees a<br>shortage (medics, engineers)",
    "In practice, 92% of<br>applicants wait longer", "Most applicants cannot<br>work as they are in detention"
  ),
  benefits = c(374, 226, 86, 217, 0, 275),
  benefits_note = c("", "", "Maximum", "", "", "")
)
origins <- list(
  c("Syria" = 23, "Serbia / Kosovo" = 14, "Eritrea" = 8),
  c("Syria" = 40, "Stateless" = 10, "Eritrea" = 8),
  c("Serbia / Kosovo" = 51, "Afghanistan" = 21, "Syria" = 16),
  c("Eritrea" = 13, "Pakistan" = 11, "Syria" = 8),
  c("Mexico" = 12, "China" = 11, "El Salvador" = 8),
  c("China" = 19, "India" = 13, "Pakistan" = 10)
)
origin_mark <- c("", "", "", "", "", "‡")
top_app <- max(asylum[["applications"]])

cells <- data.frame(
  country = asylum[["country"]],
  applied = paste0(
    colour(format(asylum[["applications"]], big.mark = ","), swatch("blue1"), 500),
    vapply(asylum[["applications"]], bar, "", max = top_app, colour = swatch("blue1")),
    '<div style="height:1.5pt"></div>',
    vapply(asylum[["decisions"]], bar, "", max = top_app, colour = swatch("blue2 text")),
    colour(dagger(format(asylum[["decisions"]], big.mark = ","), asylum[["decisions_mark"]]), swatch("blue2 text"), 500)
  ),
  origin = vapply(seq_along(origins), function(i) {
    o <- origins[[i]]
    paste0(
      sprintf('<div class="nowrap">%s</div>', dagger(paste(names(o), o), origin_mark[i])),
      vapply(o, bar, "", max = 51, colour = swatch("gold"), height = 2.5),
      collapse = ""
    )
  }, ""),
  accepted = mapply(doughnut, asylum[["accepted"]], dagger(asylum[["accepted"]], asylum[["accepted_mark"]])),
  wait = paste0(
    ifelse(asylum[["wait"]] == "", "", sprintf('<div style="font-weight:500">%s</div>', asylum[["wait"]])),
    vapply(asylum[["wait_months"]], dashes, ""),
    sprintf('<div class="nowrap">%s</div>', detail(asylum[["wait_note"]]))
  ),
  benefits = ifelse(
    asylum[["benefits"]] == 0,
    colour("<i>Nil</i>", swatch("navy")),
    paste0(
      '<div style="display:flex;gap:2pt;align-items:flex-start">',
      colour(paste0("€", asylum[["benefits"]]), swatch("navy"), 500),
      vapply(round(asylum[["benefits"]] / 10), dots, ""),
      "</div>",
      ifelse(
        asylum[["benefits_note"]] == "", "",
        colour(paste0("<i>", asylum[["benefits_note"]], "</i>"), swatch("navy"))
      )
    )
  )
)

gt::gt(cells, id = "what-to-expect") |>
  gt::fmt_markdown(gt::everything()) |>
  gt::cols_label(
    country = "Country",
    applied = gt::html(paste0(
      colour("Applications*", swatch("blue1"), 500), "<br>", colour("Decisions made", swatch("blue2 text"), 500)
    )),
    origin = gt::html("Mainly from<br>%"),
    accepted = gt::html("Accepted<br>%"),
    wait = gt::html("Minimum wait before<br>permitted to work"),
    benefits = gt::html("State benefits<br>per month")
  ) |>
  gt::cols_align("left") |>
  gt::cols_align("center", accepted) |>
  gt::cols_width(
    country ~ "32pt", applied ~ "58pt", origin ~ "62pt", accepted ~ "34pt", wait ~ "90pt", benefits ~ "56pt"
  ) |>
  gt::tab_header(econ_heading("What to expect", "Asylum processes, selected countries, 2014")) |>
  gt::tab_source_note(econ_source(
    "Sources: UNHCR; government statistics;<br><i>The Economist</i>",
    "*From UNHCR 2014 report<br>†From UNHCR Statistical Database ‡2012-13 figures"
  )) |>
  econ_table("what-to-expect", width = 332) |>
  gt::tab_style(rule_light, gt::cells_body(rows = 1:5)) |>
  gt::tab_style(rule_heavy, gt::cells_body(rows = 6))
```

## Pie / doughnut

> **NOTE: Use with caution.**
> Should probably be abandoned
> in favour of stacked bar
> if over 4 categories

In practice, the Economist stopped using pie and doughnut charts.

### The standard color order, one to six segments

```{r pie-order, econ_size = "two_column", econ_height = 150}
## Segment shares (%), clockwise from 12 o'clock; "O" is the pale "Other".
pie_shares <- list(
  c(`1` = 55.6, O = 44.4),
  c(`1` = 55.6, `2` = 44.4),
  c(`1` = 38.9, `2` = 16.7, `3` = 44.4),
  c(`1` = 22.2, `2` = 20.3, `4` = 13.1, `3` = 44.4),
  c(`1` = 22.2, `2` = 20.3, `5` = 7.4, `4` = 5.7, `3` = 44.4),
  c(`1` = 15.6, `2` = 13.3, `5` = 10.2, `3` = 11.2, `4` = 5.3, `6` = 44.4)
)
pie_demo <- do.call(rbind, lapply(seq_along(pie_shares), function(i) {
  hi <- cumsum(pie_shares[[i]])
  data.frame(
    panel = as.character(i),
    key = names(hi),
    lo = hi - pie_shares[[i]],
    hi = unname(hi)
  )
}))

pie_grid <- function(hole) {
  ggplot(pie_demo, aes(xmin = hole, xmax = 1, ymin = .data$lo, ymax = .data$hi, fill = .data$key)) +
    geom_rect() +
    coord_polar(theta = "y") +
    scale_x_continuous(limits = c(0, 1), expand = c(0, 0)) +
    scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0, 100), expand = c(0, 0)) +
    facet_wrap(~panel, nrow = 1) +
    scale_fill_manual(values = c(setNames(pal_pie(6), as.character(1:6)), O = "#CCD8DD"), guide = "none") +
    labs(x = NULL, y = NULL) +
    theme_economist_2017("print", base_size = 7) +
    theme(
      axis.text = element_blank(), axis.ticks = element_blank(),
      axis.line = element_blank(), panel.grid.major = element_blank(),
      strip.text = element_text(face = "bold", size = rel(1.2), hjust = 0.5),
      panel.spacing.x = unit(8, "pt")
    )
}

## Doughnut (hole) above, pie below -- the guide shows both rows.
pie_grid(0.52) + labs(title = "Standard colour order")
```

```{r naan, econ_height = 155}
## Doughnuts labelled directly, in the guide's own coordinates.
donut_polygons <- function(values, cx, cy, r_out, r_in, n = 40) {
  edge <- 2 * pi * c(0, cumsum(values)) / sum(values)
  do.call(rbind, lapply(seq_along(values), function(i) {
    arc <- seq(edge[i], edge[i + 1], length.out = n)
    data.frame(
      segment = names(values)[i],
      x = c(cx + r_out * sin(arc), cx + r_in * sin(rev(arc))),
      y = c(cy - r_out * cos(arc), cy - r_in * cos(rev(arc)))
    )
  }))
}

## Clockwise from 12 o'clock, as the guide draws them.
workforce <- c(
  "Jaguar Land Rover" = 19.0, "Tata Consultancy Services" = 4.9, "TGB (drinks)" = 0.7,
  "Tata Chemicals" = 0.5, "Taj (hotels)" = 0.4, "Others" = 0.6, "Tata Steel" = 19.4
)
naan_cols <- c(
  "Jaguar Land Rover" = pal_pie(1), "Tata Consultancy Services" = pal_pie(6)[6],
  "TGB (drinks)" = pal_pie(4)[4], "Tata Chemicals" = pal_pie(3)[3], "Taj (hotels)" = pal_pie(5)[5],
  "Others" = "#97AFBA", "Tata Steel" = pal_pie(2)[2]
)
naan_labels <- data.frame(
  segment = names(workforce),
  label = c("Jaguar Land\nRover 19.0", "Tata\nConsultancy\nServices 4.9", "TGB (drinks) 0.7",
            "Tata Chemicals 0.5", "Taj (hotels)\n0.4", "Others\n0.6", "Tata Steel\n19.4"),
  x = c(628, 628, 628, 58, 58, 58, 58),
  y = c(234, 438, 565, 565, 456, 344, 234),
  hjust = c(1, 1, 1, 0, 0, 0, 0),
  block_x = c(640, 640, 640, 35, 35, 35, 35),
  block_lo = c(205, 390, 552, 552, 430, 318, 205),
  block_hi = c(240, 425, 576, 576, 465, 350, 240)
)
naan_lines <- data.frame(
  id = rep(1:7, c(3, 4, 4, 4, 4, 6, 3)),
  x = c(
    652, 652, 475,
    652, 652, 380, 380,
    652, 652, 318, 318,
    35, 35, 305, 305,
    35, 35, 296, 296,
    35, 35, 205, 205, 288, 288,
    35, 35, 212
  ),
  y = c(
    240, 287, 287,
    425, 530, 530, 495,
    576, 589, 589, 487,
    576, 589, 589, 486,
    465, 497, 497, 484,

naan <- ggplot() +
  geom_path(data = naan_lines, aes(.data$x, -.data$y, group = .data$id), colour = grid_col, linewidth = 0.25) +
  geom_polygon(
    data = donut_polygons(workforce, 344, 340, 143, 71) |> transform(y = -y),
    aes(.data$x, .data$y, group = .data$segment, fill = .data$segment)
  ) +
  geom_rect(
    data = naan_labels,
    aes(
      xmin = .data$block_x, xmax = .data$block_x + 12,
      ymin = -.data$block_hi, ymax = -.data$block_lo, fill = .data$segment
    )
  ) +
  geom_text(
    data = naan_labels,
    aes(.data$x, -.data$y, label = .data$label, hjust = .data$hjust),
    size = 2.1, lineheight = 0.95
  ) +
  annotate("text", x = 344, y = -340, label = "Total\n45.4", size = 2.4, fontface = "bold", lineheight = 1) +

  theme(

  )

economist_2017_chart(
  naan +

  media = "print"
)
```

> Where linking lines get too crowded, key the labels with small colour block

```{r scramble, econ_size = "two_column", econ_height = 178}
## Drawn in the pixel coordinates of the guide's original, as for "Naan bigger".
trade <- c(
  "China*" = 156.4, "United States" = 72.1, "France" = 61.6, "India" = 57.0, "Spain" = 48.1, "Italy" = 40.9,
  "Germany" = 40.4, "Britain" = 34.4, "Japan" = 25.3, "Brazil" = 25.3, "Rest of world" = 453.8
)
investment <- c(
  "Britain" = 7.5, "United States" = 3.7, "Italy" = 3.6, "China" = 2.5, "France" = 2.1, "India" = 1.8,
  "Rest of world" = 38.1
)
## The printed entries total $1,015.3bn, which the guide rounds to $1.02trn, and $59.3bn.
stopifnot(all.equal(sum(trade), 1015.3), all.equal(sum(investment), 59.3))

## Pie order 1-6, then the guide's trade key continues to the pale grey.
trade_cols <- c(pal_pie(6), swatch("mauve"), swatch("dark teal"), swatch("olive"), swatch("grey text"), "#AABDC6")
investment_cols <- c(pal_pie(6)[c(1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 5)], "#AABDC6")

wedges <- rbind(
  transform(donut_polygons(trade, 299, 440, 182, 91), panel = "trade", fill = trade_cols[match(segment, names(trade))]),
  transform(
    donut_polygons(investment, 991, 440, 181, 90),
    panel = "investment", fill = investment_cols[match(segment, names(investment))]
  )
)
wedges$y <- -wedges$y
wedges$group <- paste(wedges$panel, wedges$segment)

## Key blocks and labels: x, y are pixel positions of the label's anchor edge.
key_row <- function(panel, segment, label, x, y, block_x, colour, hjust) {
  data.frame(panel, segment, label, x, y, block_x, colour, hjust)
}
labels <- rbind(
  key_row("trade", names(trade)[1:8], paste(names(trade)[1:8], sprintf("%.1f", trade[1:8])), 636,
          c(207, 271, 336, 401, 466, 530, 595, 660), 641, trade_cols[1:8], 1),
  key_row("trade", "Rest of world", "Rest of world\n453.8", 52, 207, 30, trade_cols[11], 0),
  key_row("trade", "Brazil", "Brazil\n25.3", 52, 570, 30, trade_cols[10], 0),
  key_row("trade", "Japan", "Japan 25.3", 52, 660, 30, trade_cols[9], 0),
  key_row("investment", names(investment)[1:6],
          paste0(names(investment)[1:6], "\n", sprintf("%.1f", investment[1:6])), 1346,
          c(208, 293, 378, 461, 544, 628), 1355, investment_cols[1:6], 1),
  key_row("investment", "Rest of world", "Rest of world\n38.1", 770, 207, 750, investment_cols[7], 0)
)
labels$row <- ifelse(grepl("\n", labels$label), 38, 36)
leaders <- data.frame(
  id = rep(1:6, c(3, 3, 4, 2, 4, 3)),
  x = c(
    1058, 1058, 1262,
    1140, 1140, 1178,
    1170, 1220, 1220, 1262,
    1172, 1275,
    1160, 1218, 1218, 1262,
    1140, 1140, 1285
  ),
  y = c(
    258, 207, 207,
    330, 293, 293,
    412, 412, 378, 378,
    462, 462,
    508, 508, 544, 544,
    540, 628, 628
  )
)
headings <- data.frame(
  x = c(35, 752),
  label = c("bold('Goods trade with Africa,')~'2013, $bn'",
            "bold('Foreign direct investment in Africa,')~'2012, $bn'")
)
centres <- data.frame(x = c(299, 991), label = c("Total\n$1.02trn", "Total\n$59.3bn"))

scramble <- ggplot() +
  geom_path(data = leaders, aes(.data$x, -.data$y, group = .data$id), colour = grid_col, linewidth = 0.2) +
  geom_polygon(data = wedges, aes(.data$x, .data$y, group = .data$group, fill = I(.data$fill))) +
  geom_rect(
    data = labels,
    aes(
      xmin = .data$block_x, xmax = .data$block_x + 12, ymin = -.data$y - .data$row / 2, ymax = -.data$y + .data$row / 2,
      fill = I(.data$colour)
    )
  ) +
  geom_text(
    data = labels,
    aes(.data$x, -.data$y - ifelse(grepl("\n", .data$label), 16, 0), label = .data$label, hjust = .data$hjust),
    size = 2.1, lineheight = 0.95, vjust = 0.5
  ) +
  geom_text(data = centres, aes(.data$x, -440, label = .data$label), size = 2.4, fontface = "bold", lineheight = 1) +
  geom_text(
    data = headings, aes(.data$x, -145, label = .data$label), parse = TRUE, hjust = 0, size = 2.1
  ) +
  geom_segment(
    data = data.frame(x = c(35, 752)), aes(x = .data$x, xend = .data$x + 42, y = -118, yend = -118),
    colour = econ_red, linewidth = 0.5
  ) +
  coord_fixed(xlim = c(25, 1385), ylim = c(-690, -100), expand = FALSE) +
  labs(title = "The scramble in Africa", x = NULL, y = NULL) +
  theme_economist_2017("print", base_size = 7) +
  theme(
    axis.text = element_blank(), axis.ticks = element_blank(),
    axis.line = element_blank(), panel.grid.major = element_blank()
  )

economist_2017_chart(
  scramble +
    labs(caption = "Sources: UNCTAD; IMF"),
  media = "print",
  footnote = "*Including Macau and Hong Kong"
)
```

## Double-scale charts

> Double scales can be good at showing correlations and are economical with space. **But they can also be confusing/misleading.** 

Axis labels are colored to match their series: cyan and teal for axis 1, maroon and mauve for axis 2.
`sec_axis()` rescales the second series onto the first axis.
Both axes use `guide_axis_economist_2017()` to place their titles above them.

### One line on each axis

```{r out-of-steam, econ_height = 175}
## Series in pixel coordinates, converted to years and values.
px_year <- function(x) 1955 + (x - 115) / 8
px_value <- function(y) (633 - y) / 5.27
track_px <- data.frame(
  x = c(115, 140, 155, 172, 190, 205, 220, 240, 300, 420, 430, 450, 470, 500, 520, 588),
  y = c(508, 509, 511, 520, 535, 548, 553, 557, 558, 558, 553, 553, 553, 553, 557, 556)
)
passengers_px <- data.frame(
  x = c(115, 131, 148, 160, 172, 190, 205, 220, 237, 250, 262, 272, 285, 298, 312, 322, 333, 340, 353, 365, 378,
        395, 410, 428, 440, 455, 470, 480, 490, 505, 520, 535, 548, 560, 575, 588),
  y = c(458, 442, 445, 452, 465, 467, 478, 482, 472, 485, 475, 470, 483, 475, 465, 478, 490, 480, 478, 470, 457,
        460, 468, 480, 465, 450, 430, 428, 420, 412, 390, 370, 360, 335, 318, 302)
)
rail <- rbind(
  data.frame(series = "track", year = px_year(track_px$x), value = px_value(track_px$y)),
  data.frame(series = "passengers", year = px_year(passengers_px$x), value = px_value(passengers_px$y))
)
maroon <- pal_dot(6)[2]
cyan <- pal_dot(6)[1]
cyan_text <- swatch("blue2 text")
slate <- "#6B7F8C"

steam <- ggplot(rail, aes(.data$year, .data$value, colour = .data$series)) +
  geom_segment(
    x = 1994, xend = 1994, y = 0, yend = 64, linetype = "22", linewidth = 0.25, colour = slate
  ) +
  annotate("text", x = 1994, y = 66.5, label = "Privatisation begins", size = 1.9, colour = slate) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.9) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c(track = maroon, passengers = cyan), guide = "none") +
  scale_y_continuous(
    guide = guide_axis_economist_2017(),
    name = "National rail track\n'000 km", limits = c(0, 70), breaks = seq(0, 70, 10), expand = c(0, 0),
    sec.axis = sec_axis(
      ~., name = "Passenger kilometres\nbn", breaks = seq(0, 70, 10), guide = guide_axis_economist_2017()
    )
  ) +
  scale_x_continuous(
    breaks = c(1955, 1970, 1980, 1990, 2000, 2014),
    labels = c("1955", "70", "80", "90", "2000", "14"), limits = c(1945, 2022), expand = c(0, 0)
  ) +
  labs(title = "Out of steam", subtitle = "Britain, railways", x = NULL) +
  theme_economist_2017("print", base_size = 7) +
  theme(
    axis.text.y.left = element_text(colour = maroon),
    axis.text.y.right = element_text(colour = cyan_text),
    axis.title.y.left = element_text(colour = maroon, hjust = 0),
    axis.title.y.right = element_text(colour = cyan_text, hjust = 1)
  )

economist_2017_chart(
  steam +
    labs(caption = "Source: Department for Transport"),
  media = "print"
)
```

### Three lines on the left-hand axis

```{r golden-triangle, econ_height = 165}
## As for "Out of steam"; the trade series is on the left scale.
px_year <- function(x) 1994 + (x - 132) / 20.5
px_value <- function(y) (591 - y) / 3.69
trace <- function(series, xy) {
  data.frame(series = series, year = px_year(xy[[1]]), value = px_value(xy[[2]]))
}
nafta <- rbind(
  trace("Mexico", list(
    c(130, 150, 172, 195, 215, 235, 255, 280, 300, 320, 340, 360, 380, 400, 420, 440, 460, 480, 500, 520, 540, 565),
    c(268, 274, 273, 268, 262, 258, 255, 257, 260, 261, 262, 268, 272, 280, 286, 280, 283, 290, 293, 290, 285, 282)
  )),
  trace("Canada", list(
    c(130, 150, 172, 195, 215, 235, 255, 280, 300, 320, 340, 360, 380, 400, 420, 440, 460, 480, 500, 520, 540, 565),
    c(285, 292, 285, 282, 272, 266, 265, 264, 266, 270, 273, 277, 284, 296, 300, 308, 311, 314, 310, 306, 303, 302)
  )),
  trace("United States", list(
    c(130, 150, 172, 195, 215, 235, 255, 280, 300, 320, 340, 360, 380, 400, 420, 440, 460, 480, 500, 520, 540, 565),
    c(471, 480, 478, 470, 463, 457, 455, 457, 455, 456, 455, 455, 462, 469, 473, 474, 471, 470, 469, 467, 464, 463)
  )),
  trace("Total trilateral trade", list(
    c(130, 150, 172, 195, 215, 235, 255, 275, 295, 315, 335, 355, 375, 395, 415, 440, 462, 480, 500, 520, 545, 565),
    c(498, 483, 473, 460, 441, 431, 414, 388, 400, 403, 396, 375, 350, 327, 312, 299, 372, 312, 280, 265, 258, 244)
  ))
)
nafta$series <- factor(
  nafta$series,
  levels = c("Mexico", "Canada", "United States", "Total trilateral trade")
)
cyan_text <- swatch("blue2 text")
nafta_cols <- c(
  Mexico = pal_dot(6)[1], Canada = pal_dot(6)[5], `United States` = pal_dot(6)[1],
  `Total trilateral trade` = pal_dot(6)[2]
)

golden <- ggplot(nafta, aes(.data$year, .data$value, colour = .data$series)) +
  geom_line(aes(linewidth = .data$series == "Total trilateral trade")) +
  scale_linewidth_manual(values = c(`FALSE` = 0.7, `TRUE` = 0.9), guide = "none") +
  geom_text(
    data = data.frame(
      year = c(px_year(133), px_year(133), px_year(556)), value = px_value(c(242, 316, 495)),
      hjust = c(0, 0, 1), series = factor(c("Mexico", "Canada", "United States"), levels = levels(nafta$series))
    ),
    aes(label = .data$series, hjust = .data$hjust), size = 2.3, show.legend = FALSE
  ) +
  scale_y_continuous(
    guide = guide_axis_economist_2017(),
    name = "NAFTA countries' exports\nto each other, % of total", limits = c(0, 100), breaks = seq(0, 100, 20),
    expand = c(0, 0),
    sec.axis = sec_axis(
      ~ . * 1.25 / 100, name = "Total trilateral trade\n$trn", breaks = seq(0, 1.25, 0.25),
      labels = c("0", "0.25", "0.50", "0.75", "1.00", "1.25"), guide = guide_axis_economist_2017()
    )
  ) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = nafta_cols, guide = "none") +
  scale_x_continuous(
    breaks = c(1994, 2000, 2005, 2010, 2015), labels = c("1994", "2000", "05", "10", "15"),
    limits = c(1989.3, 2019.3), expand = c(0, 0)
  ) +
  labs(title = "Golden triangle", x = NULL) +
  theme_economist_2017("print", base_size = 7) +
  theme(
    axis.text.y.left = element_text(colour = cyan_text),
    axis.text.y.right = element_text(colour = pal_dot(6)[2]),
    axis.title.y.left = element_text(colour = cyan_text, hjust = 0),
    axis.title.y.right = element_text(colour = pal_dot(6)[2], hjust = 1)
  )

economist_2017_chart(
  golden +
    labs(caption = "Sources: Thomson Reuters; IMF"),
  media = "print"
)
```

### Line and column

> Always choose the axis colour order that will visually associate the
> labels best with the corresponding line

```{r chavismo, econ_height = 175}
venezuela <- data.frame(
  year = 2004:2016,
  gdp = c(18.3, 10.3, 9.9, 8.8, 5.3, -3.2, -1.5, 4.2, 5.6, 1.3, -3.9, -5.7, -18.6),
  prices = c(22, 16, 14, 19, 31, 27, 29, 26, 21, 41, 70, 180, 800)
)
cyan_text <- swatch("blue2 text")

chavismo <- ggplot(venezuela, aes(year)) +
  geom_col(aes(y = gdp), fill = pal_dot(6)[1], width = 0.78) +
  geom_line(aes(y = prices * 20 / 800), colour = pal_dot(6)[2], linewidth = 0.9) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, colour = econ_red, linewidth = 0.2) +
  scale_y_continuous(
    guide = guide_axis_economist_2017(),
    name = "GDP", limits = c(-20, 20), breaks = seq(-20, 20, 5), expand = c(0, 0),
    sec.axis = sec_axis(
      ~ . * 800 / 20, name = "Consumer prices, year-end", breaks = seq(-800, 800, 200),
      guide = guide_axis_economist_2017()
    )
  ) +
  scale_x_continuous(
    breaks = seq(2004, 2016, 2), labels = c("2004", "06", "08", "10", "12", "14", "16*"),
    limits = c(2001.6, 2018.8), expand = c(0, 0)
  ) +
  labs(title = "Chavismo in action",
       subtitle = "Venezuela, % change on a year earlier", x = NULL) +
  theme_economist_2017("print", base_size = 7) +
  theme(
    axis.title.y.left = element_text(colour = cyan_text, hjust = 0),
    axis.title.y.right = element_text(colour = pal_dot(6)[2], hjust = 1),
    axis.text.y.left = element_text(colour = cyan_text),
    axis.text.y.right = element_text(colour = pal_dot(6)[2])
  )

economist_2017_chart(
  chavismo +
    labs(caption = "Sources: IMF; Reuters"),
  media = "print",
  footnote = "*Preliminary estimate"
)
```

### What to avoid

> Double scales can be good at showing correlations and are economical with space.
> **But they can also be confusing/misleading.**
> Here are some things to avoid when considering a double scale
> 
> **If you cannot conform to the above rules try splitting the chart into panels or indexing the variables.**

> :cross: Avoid breaking the scales without good reason
> 
> Broken scale distorts data

```{r double-scale-avoid, econ_height = 155}
## Monthly series; the right scale (yields, %) runs 0-5, so the zero lines differ.
px_euro <- function(y) 1 + (473 - y) / 660
months <- 2013.5 + (0:23) / 12
qe <- rbind(
  data.frame(series = "Euro", year = months, value = px_euro(c(
    247, 245, 234, 236, 243, 250, 255, 268, 294, 310, 322, 333, 380, 397, 432, 432, 408, 405, 420, 411, 404, 404,
    438, 428
  ))),
  data.frame(series = "Italy", year = months, value = px_euro(c(
    284, 305, 324, 332, 344, 351, 367, 372, 392, 400, 392, 420, 430, 445, 465, 468, 450, 418, 402, 435, 420, 433,
    441, 458
  ))),
  data.frame(series = "Euro area", year = months[1:23], value = px_euro(c(
    337, 346, 358, 376, 380, 398, 406, 418, 427, 438, 442, 455, 465, 468, 486, 491, 458, 440, 450, 457, 450, 468,
    472
  )))
)
qe_cols <- c(Euro = pal_dot(6)[2], Italy = pal_dot(6)[5], `Euro area` = pal_dot(6)[1])
cyan_text <- swatch("blue2 text")

quantifying <- ggplot(qe, aes(.data$year, .data$value, colour = .data$series)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.9) +
  annotate("text", x = 2014.0, y = 1.24, label = "Italy", colour = pal_dot(6)[5], size = 2.4, fontface = "bold") +
  annotate("text", x = 2014.05, y = 1.03, label = "Euro area", colour = pal_dot(6)[1], size = 2.4, fontface = "bold") +
  scale_colour_manual(values = qe_cols, guide = "none") +
  scale_y_continuous(
    guide = guide_axis_economist_2017(),
    name = "Euro against the\ndollar, $ per €", limits = c(0.9, 1.4001), breaks = seq(1, 1.4, 0.1),
    labels = function(x) sprintf("%.1f", x), expand = c(0, 0),
    sec.axis = sec_axis(
      ~ (. - 0.9) * 10, name = "Ten-year government-\nbond yields, %", breaks = 0:5,
      guide = guide_axis_economist_2017()
    )
  ) +
  scale_x_continuous(
    breaks = c(2014, 2015), labels = c("2014", "2015"), limits = c(2013.19, 2015.69), expand = c(0, 0)
  ) +
  labs(title = "Quantifying QE", x = NULL) +
  theme_economist_2017("print", base_size = 7) +
  theme(
    axis.text.y.left = element_text(colour = pal_dot(6)[2]),
    axis.text.y.right = element_text(colour = cyan_text),
    axis.title.y.left = element_text(colour = pal_dot(6)[2], hjust = 0),
    axis.title.y.right = element_text(colour = cyan_text, hjust = 1)
  )

economist_2017_chart(
  quantifying +
    labs(caption = "Source: Thomson Reuters"),
  media = "print"
)
```

```{r double-scale-avoid-2, econ_height = 155}
## Annual bars, 2002-15, and the oil price on the right scale.
beneath <- data.frame(
  year = 2002:2015,
  cash = c(27, 68, 75, 98, 79, 90, 91, -5, 32, 31, 18, -30, 1, -50)
)
brent_px <- data.frame(
  x = c(100, 130, 165, 190, 205, 225, 237, 258, 275, 285, 295, 302, 310, 318, 324, 340, 358, 375, 385, 395, 405,
        418, 430, 440, 455, 470, 485, 500, 510, 520, 530, 540, 550, 560, 575, 590),
  y = c(512, 495, 468, 455, 455, 420, 415, 430, 375, 370, 320, 290, 385, 470, 480, 420, 400, 415, 350, 320, 345,
        340, 320, 345, 335, 345, 340, 340, 345, 400, 440, 430, 455, 480, 460, 450)
)
brent <- data.frame(
  year = 2002 + (brent_px$x - 100) / 33.7,
  price = (538 - brent_px$y) / 1.88
)
cyan_text <- swatch("blue2 text")

## The right-hand scale is the left shifted by 60, so the two zero lines do not coincide.
lies <- ggplot() +
  geom_col(data = beneath, aes(.data$year, .data$cash), fill = pal_dot(6)[1], width = 0.66) +
  geom_line(data = brent, aes(.data$year, .data$price - 60), colour = pal_dot(6)[2], linewidth = 0.9) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, colour = econ_red, linewidth = 0.2) +
  scale_y_continuous(
    guide = guide_axis_economist_2017(),
    name = "Big oil companies' enterprise\nfree cash flow, $bn",
    limits = c(-60, 120), breaks = seq(-60, 120, 30), labels = function(x) abs(x), expand = c(0, 0),
    sec.axis = sec_axis(
      ~ . + 60, name = "Oil price\nBrent, $ per barrel", breaks = seq(0, 180, 30),
      guide = guide_axis_economist_2017()
    )
  ) +
  scale_x_continuous(
    breaks = seq(2002, 2016, 2), labels = c("2002", "04", "06", "08", "10", "12", "14", "16"),
    limits = c(2000.1, 2018.3), expand = c(0, 0)
  ) +
  labs(title = "What lies beneath", x = NULL) +
  theme_economist_2017("print", base_size = 7) +
  theme(
    axis.text.y.left = element_text(colour = cyan_text),
    axis.text.y.right = element_text(colour = pal_dot(6)[2]),
    axis.title.y.left = element_text(colour = cyan_text, hjust = 0),
    axis.title.y.right = element_text(colour = pal_dot(6)[2], hjust = 1)
  )

economist_2017_chart(
  lies +
    labs(caption = "Source: BCG"),
  media = "print"
)
```

```{r double-scale-avoid-3, econ_height = 165}
## Daily series.
rand_px <- data.frame(
  x = c(88, 95, 110, 125, 133, 140, 150, 160, 172, 185, 200, 215, 228, 240, 255, 270, 285, 300, 315, 330, 345,
        360, 375, 390, 405, 420, 435, 450, 465, 480, 495, 510, 520, 530, 540, 550, 560, 575, 582),
  y = c(258, 290, 290, 300, 375, 340, 360, 300, 290, 272, 275, 270, 265, 258, 262, 252, 262, 285, 282, 320, 310,
        325, 330, 345, 350, 375, 380, 385, 370, 395, 420, 470, 520, 550, 490, 470, 480, 460, 480)
)
sacci_px <- data.frame(
  x = c(88, 110, 125, 140, 150, 160, 172, 180, 200, 210, 225, 237, 250, 262, 272, 285, 300, 315, 330, 345, 360,
        375, 385, 395, 410, 420, 435, 445, 460, 475, 485, 500, 515, 525, 535, 545, 555, 570, 580),
  y = c(285, 295, 330, 300, 350, 330, 290, 300, 300, 290, 240, 235, 255, 230, 245, 270, 280, 285, 350, 330, 340,
        370, 365, 355, 350, 365, 348, 340, 360, 385, 345, 395, 410, 470, 490, 480, 455, 470, 475)
)
zuma <- rbind(
  data.frame(series = "rand", year = 2008 + (rand_px$x - 88) / 55, value = 6 + (rand_px$y - 228) / 30),
  data.frame(series = "sacci", year = 2008 + (sacci_px$x - 88) / 55, value = 6 + (sacci_px$y - 228) / 30)
)
cyan_text <- swatch("blue2 text")

## An index value against an inverted currency scale: two disparate measures
## forced into visual correlation.
zuma_plot <- ggplot(zuma, aes(.data$year, .data$value, colour = .data$series)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 12, colour = econ_red, linewidth = 0.2) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.8) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c(rand = pal_dot(6)[2], sacci = pal_dot(6)[1]), guide = "none") +
  scale_y_reverse(
    guide = guide_axis_economist_2017(),
    name = "Rand per $, inverted scale", limits = c(18, 6), breaks = seq(6, 18, 3), expand = c(0, 0),
    sec.axis = sec_axis(
      ~ 120 - (. - 6) * 40 / 12, name = "SACCI Business\nConfidence Index,\n2015=100", breaks = seq(80, 120, 10),
      guide = guide_axis_economist_2017()
    )
  ) +
  scale_x_continuous(
    breaks = 2008.5 + 0:8, labels = c("2008", sprintf("%02d", 9:16)), limits = c(2007.04, 2018.2), expand = c(0, 0)
  ) +
  labs(title = "The Zuma years", subtitle = "South Africa", x = NULL) +
  theme_economist_2017("print", base_size = 7) +
  theme(
    axis.text.y.left = element_text(colour = pal_dot(6)[2]),
    axis.text.y.right = element_text(colour = cyan_text),
    axis.title.y.left = element_text(colour = pal_dot(6)[2], hjust = 0),
    axis.title.y.right = element_text(colour = cyan_text, hjust = 1)
  )

economist_2017_chart(
  zuma_plot +
    labs(caption = "Sources: Thomson Reuters; SACCI"),
  media = "print"
)
```

## Blob heads

> A secondary data variable added as area-sized bubbles or number boxes. Can be used with column or thermometer charts.

### Numbers inside the bubbles

```{r big-mac, econ_height = 335}
## Values from the guide's marks.
bigmac <- data.frame(
  country = c("Switzerland", "Norway", "Sweden", "Brazil", "United States",
              "Euro area", "Britain", "Japan", "Turkey", "China",
              "Vietnam", "India", "Mexico", "Russia"),
  y2016 = c(31, 6, 5, -32, -1, -19, -14, -37, -31, -46, -48, -61, -43, -68),
  y2017 = c(27, 14, 4, 2, 0, -19, -24, -35, -41, -43, -45, -50, -54, -57),
  price = c(6.4, 5.8, 5.3, 5.1, 5.1, 4.1, 3.8, 3.3, 3.0, 2.8, 2.6, 2.5, 2.3, 2.2)
)
bigmac$country <- factor(bigmac$country, levels = rev(bigmac$country))
bigmac_long <- data.frame(
  country = rep(bigmac$country, 2),
  year = rep(c("January 2016", "January 2017"), each = nrow(bigmac)),
  value = c(bigmac$y2016, bigmac$y2017)
)
## Bubbles filled c22.5 k15, multiplied into the ground; diameter grows with price.
blob_fill <- grDevices::rgb(t(grDevices::col2rgb(print_numberbox) * grDevices::col2rgb(print_bg) / 255),
                            maxColorValue = 255)
bigmac$bubble <- 4.4 + 0.72 * bigmac$price

## Footnote marks hang off the country names as superscripts.
bigmac_marks <- c("United States" = "\u2020", "Euro area" = "\u2021", "China" = "\u00a7", "India" = "**")
bigmac_labels <- function(x) {
  parse(text = ifelse(x %in% names(bigmac_marks),
                      paste0("'", x, "'^'", bigmac_marks[x], "'"),
                      paste0("'", x, "'")))
}

big_mac <- ggplot(bigmac, aes(y = country)) +
  ## Light rules across each row, stopping short of the bubble column.
  geom_segment(aes(x = -80, xend = 56, yend = country), colour = grid_col, linewidth = 0.18) +
  ## Each dumbbell's bar runs back to zero.
  geom_segment(aes(x = pmin(0, y2016, y2017), xend = pmax(0, y2016, y2017), yend = country),
               colour = swatch("grey box"), linewidth = 0.34) +
  geom_linerange(
    data = bigmac_long,
    aes(x = value, ymin = as.numeric(country) - 0.2,
        ymax = as.numeric(country) + 0.2, colour = year),
    linewidth = 0.6
  ) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, colour = econ_red, linewidth = 0.2) +
  ## The blob heads: the value inside, in 7pt.
  geom_point(aes(x = 66, size = bubble), colour = blob_fill, stroke = 0) +
  geom_text(aes(x = 66, label = format(price, nsmall = 1)), size = 7 / ggplot2::.pt,
            colour = print_pal$text) +
  scale_size_identity() +
  coord_cartesian(clip = "off") +
  ## The guide labels every 20; the fallback font is too wide for that at
  ## this width, so every other gridline goes unlabelled.
  scale_x_continuous(position = "top", limits = c(-85, 84),
                     breaks = seq(-80, 40, 20), labels = c("-80", "", "-40", "", "0", "", "40")) +
  scale_y_discrete(labels = bigmac_labels) +
  scale_colour_economist_2017("print", type = "dot") +
  labs(
    title = "The Big Mac index",
    subtitle = paste0("Local currency under (-) / over (+)\nvaluation against the dollar, %\n",
                      "Right-hand figures: Big Mac price*, $"),
    x = NULL, y = NULL, colour = NULL
  ) +
  theme_economist_2017("print", horizontal = FALSE, base_size = 7)

economist_2017_chart(
  big_mac +
    ## The footnote shares the caption's row, so the caption is padded to the
    ## footnote's seven lines to reserve the room.
    labs(caption = "Sources:\nMcDonald's;\nThe Economist"),
  media = "print",
  footnote = paste0("*At market exchange rates\n(Jan 11th 2017)\n\u2020Average of four cities\n",
                    "\u2021Weighted average of\nmember countries\n\u00a7Average of five cities\n**Maharaja Mac")
)
```

### Bubbles and numbers outside the bar

> To avoid awkward alignment, if most numbers won’t fit, put them
> outside bubble and align text right

```{r up-in-air, econ_height = 254}
## Bubble values are printed.
travel <- data.frame(
  country = c("China", "India", "Germany", "Spain", "United States", "Britain",
              "South Korea", "Canada", "Brazil", "France", "Italy", "Australia",
              "Japan", "Netherlands", "Russia"),
  change = c(16.5, 9.7, 7.6, 6.7, 5.4, 5.4, 3.9, 3.8, 3.7, 2.0, 1.3, 1.3, 1.1, -1.7, -6.6),
  bn = c(261, 26, 58, 18, 288, 44, 32, 23, 32, 36, 31, 21, 62, 18, 21)
)
travel$country <- factor(travel$country, levels = rev(travel$country))

air <- ggplot(travel, aes(country, change)) +
  geom_col(aes(fill = change < 0), width = 0.65, show.legend = FALSE) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, colour = econ_red, linewidth = 0.2) +
  ## Bubbles sized by area, with the value set to their right.
  geom_point(aes(y = 22.2, size = bn), colour = blob_fill, stroke = 0, show.legend = FALSE) +
  geom_text(aes(y = 31.5, label = bn), size = 7 / ggplot2::.pt, hjust = 1,
            colour = print_pal$text) +
  ## The "$bn" key: a text block above the axis, pointing down at the bubbles.
  annotate("label_economist_2017", x = 15.7, y = 25.1, label = "$bn", pointer = "bottom", fill = blob_fill) +
  ## Fixed limits keep the key above the axis out of the panel's range.
  coord_flip(xlim = c(0.45, 15.5), ylim = c(-10.5, 31.7), expand = FALSE, clip = "off") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c(`FALSE` = pal_bar(2)[1], `TRUE` = pal_bar(2)[2])) +
  scale_size_area(max_size = 7.3) +
  ## "-10" and "-5" run together in the fallback font; leave -5 unlabelled.
  scale_y_continuous(guide = guide_axis_economist_2017(), position = "right",
                     breaks = seq(-10, 15, 5), labels = c("-10", "", "0", "5", "10", "15")) +
  labs(
    title = "Up in the air",
    subtitle = "Business travel spending, 2014\n% change on a year earlier",
    x = NULL, y = NULL
  ) +
  theme_economist_2017("print", horizontal = FALSE, base_size = 7)

economist_2017_chart(
  air +
    labs(caption = "Source: GBTA"),
  media = "print"
)
```

### Equal-sized number blocks

> If number range or positive / negative values rule out bubbles, revert to
> equal-sized number blocks

```{r starting-small, econ_height = 175}
## Market caps are printed.
exchanges <- data.frame(
  exchange = rep(c("Johannesburg", "Nigeria", "Mauritius", "Nairobi", "Namibia", "BRVM*"), 2),
  listing = rep(c("Domestic", "Foreign"), each = 6),
  listed = c(306, 176, 75, 65, 8, 41, 71, 0, 0, 0, 33, 0)
)
exchanges$exchange <- factor(exchanges$exchange, levels = rev(unique(exchanges$exchange)))
exchanges$listing <- factor(exchanges$listing, levels = c("Foreign", "Domestic"))
caps <- data.frame(
  exchange = factor(levels(exchanges$exchange), levels = levels(exchanges$exchange)),
  cap = c(11.6, 2.3, 19.9, 6.2, 29.3, 943)
)

small <- ggplot(exchanges, aes(exchange, listed)) +
  geom_col(aes(fill = listing), width = 0.65) +
  ## Equal-sized blocks, right-aligned, rather than area-sized bubbles: 9pt
  ## tall and 15pt wide.
  geom_tile(data = caps, aes(y = 500, height = 82), width = 0.6, fill = blob_fill) +
  geom_text(data = caps, aes(y = 500, label = cap), size = 7 / ggplot2::.pt, colour = print_pal$text) +
  ## The "Market cap, $bn" key: a text block pointing right at the last block.
  annotate("label_economist_2017", x = 1, y = 445, label = "Market cap, $bn", pointer = "right", fill = blob_fill) +
  coord_flip(xlim = c(0.45, 6.55), ylim = c(0, 548), expand = FALSE) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c(Domestic = pal_bar(2)[2], Foreign = pal_bar(2)[1]),
                    limits = c("Domestic", "Foreign")) +
  scale_y_continuous(guide = guide_axis_economist_2017(), position = "right", breaks = seq(0, 400, 100)) +
  labs(
    title = "Starting small",
    subtitle = "Number of companies\nlisted on stock exchanges\nOctober 2016",
    x = NULL, y = NULL, fill = NULL
  ) +
  theme_economist_2017("print", horizontal = FALSE, base_size = 7) +
  ## The key sits at the right of the subtitle, which a negative margin tucks up into.
  theme(legend.position = "top", legend.justification = "right", legend.direction = "vertical",
        legend.margin = margin(t = -28, b = 0))

economist_2017_chart(
  small +
    labs(caption = "Source: World Federation\nof Exchanges"),
  media = "print",
  footnote = "*West African\nregional exchange"
)
```

### Text blocks

`geom_label_economist_2017()` draws the guide's text blocks: 7.5pt text in a box 12pt
tall for one line and 23pt for two, with a pointer centred on one side, or
moved along it but kept 6pt from the corners. `annotate("label_economist_2017", ...)`
adds a single one.

```{r text-blocks, econ_size = "two_column", econ_height = 95}
blocks <- data.frame(
  x = c(0.9, 2.2, 1.6, 2.6, 3),
  y = c(1.9, 1.6, 0.7, 1, 2),
  label = c("ECB announces QE", "ECB announces\nQE beginning", "ECB announces QE", "ECB announces QE",
            "ECB announces QE"),
  pointer = c("bottom", "bottom", "right", "top", "left"),
  hjust = c(0.5, 0.5, 0.5, 0.15, 0.5)
)
ggplot(blocks, aes(x, y)) +
  ## One layer per pointer side; x and y are where each pointer touches.
  lapply(split(blocks, blocks$pointer), function(d) {
    geom_label_economist_2017(aes(label = label, hjust = hjust), data = d, pointer = d$pointer[1], fill = blob_fill)
  }) +
  geom_point(colour = econ_red, size = 0.6) +
  coord_cartesian(xlim = c(0.4, 4.4), ylim = c(-0.2, 3), expand = FALSE) +
  theme_economist_2017("print", base_size = 7) +
  theme_void() +
  theme(plot.background = element_rect(fill = print_bg, colour = NA))
```

## Timelines

Timelines add dated events and periods to a chart of a year axis. ggthemes has
a layer for each part:

* `geom_event_economist_2017()`: a specific date event, a rule with an arrowhead
  up (or down) to its label;
* `geom_span_economist_2017()`: a time period in the panel, shaded, with its label
  over a rule along the top;
* `geom_period_economist_2017()`: thin bars of alternating color below the axis
  for successive periods, such as terms of office;
* `geom_year_band_economist_2017()`: the band of year cells that serves as the
  x-axis.

All four take positions in data units and sizes in points.

```{r timeline-setup}
## Timelines put their own band, periods and labels where an axis would be.
timeline_theme <- function() {
  theme(
    axis.text = element_blank(), axis.ticks = element_blank(), axis.line = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.major = element_blank()
  )
}
## Gridlines broken to short stubs at either side, "to avoid chart area
## becoming too crowded", with their values above them.
gridline_stubs <- function(y, left, right, width, labels_left = y, labels_right = NULL, colour = grid_col) {
  list(
    annotate("segment", x = left, xend = left + width, y = y, yend = y, colour = colour, linewidth = 0.2),
    annotate("segment", x = right - width, xend = right, y = y, yend = y, colour = colour, linewidth = 0.2),
    if (!is.null(labels_left)) {
      annotate("text", x = left, y = y, label = labels_left, hjust = 0, vjust = -0.3, size = 6.5 / ggplot2::.pt)
    },
    if (!is.null(labels_right)) {
      annotate("text", x = right, y = y, label = labels_right, hjust = 1, vjust = -0.3, size = 6.5 / ggplot2::.pt)
    }
  )
}
pt_line <- function(pt) pt / 0.75 / ggplot2::.pt
tl_blue1 <- swatch("blue1")
tl_maroon <- swatch("maroon")
```

### Non-data timeline

> Use thin alternating-colour bars to mark out time periods. Key repeated
> events, like coup attempts, to avoid duplicating text labels

```{r philippines, econ_size = "two_column", econ_height = 192}
## Heights here are in points above the year band.
philippines_events <- data.frame(
  year = c(1965.89, 1983.58, 1986.22, 1987.20, 1988.46, 1997.45, 2001.10, 2007.63, 2009.44, 2011.76),
  from = c(2, 27.8, 27.8, 2, 2, 2, 2, 2, 2, 2),
  to = c(39.7, 56, 64.7, 48.4, 36.4, 17.8, 69.1, 31.4, 46.6, 26.8),
  label = c(
    "Ferdinand\nMarcos\nelected", "Benigno Aquino Jr.\nassassinated on\nreturn from US exile", "Marcos ousted",
    "New constitution", "Duterte first\nelected mayor\nof Davao", "Asian\nfinancial\ncrisis\nstarts",
    "Joseph Estrada resigns\nduring impeachment\nproceedings", "Estrada\nconvicted of\ncorruption",
    "Corazon Aquino\ndies", "Ms Arroyo\narrested"
  ),
  hjust = c(0, 1, 0, 0, 0, 0.5, 0, 1, 0, 0)
)
presidents <- data.frame(
  start = c(1965.96, 1985.68, 1991.91, 1997.83, 2000.46, 2009.66, 2016.32),
  end = c(1985.53, 1991.76, 1997.68, 2000.31, 2009.51, 2016.23, 2016.89),
  ## Gloria Arroyo's name starts a line down, clear of Estrada's.
  label = c("Marcos", "Corazon\nAquino", "Ramos", "Estrada", "\nGloria\nMacapagal\nArroyo", "Benigno\nAquino III", "")
)
philippines_coups <- c(1986.62, 1987.06, 1987.58, 1989.75, 1990.23, 1990.76, 2003.50, 2006.24, 2007.80)

philippines <- ggplot() +
  ## Martial law and the "People Power" revolution, as thin blue spans.
  annotate(
    "span_economist_2017", xmin = c(1972.46, 1983.50), xmax = c(1981.19, 1986.26), ymin = 1.6, ymax = 2.6,
    label = c("Marcos imposes\nmartial law", "“People\nPower”\nrevolution"),
    fill = tl_blue1, colour = tl_blue1, text_colour = tl_blue1, linewidth = 0
  ) +
  geom_event_economist_2017(
    aes(x = year, y = from, yend = to, label = label, hjust = hjust),
    data = philippines_events, colour = tl_blue1
  ) +
  geom_year_band_economist_2017(from = 1965, to = 2016, height = 15) +
  ## Coup attempts are keyed, not labelled: a dot on the band for each.
  annotate("point", x = philippines_coups, y = -15, shape = 21, size = 4.5 / ggplot2::.pt, stroke = 0.3,
           fill = swatch("grey text"), colour = print_bg) +
  geom_period_economist_2017(
    aes(xmin = start, xmax = end, y = -18.7, label = label), data = presidents, fontface = "bold"
  ) +
  annotate("point", x = c(1969.60, 1981.30, 2004.51), y = -22.4, shape = 25, size = 4.8 / ggplot2::.pt,
           fill = tl_maroon, colour = tl_maroon, stroke = 0) +
  annotate("text", x = c(1985.68, 2009.66) + 0.1, y = c(-38.6, -38.6), vjust = 1, hjust = 0,
           label = c("Wife of Benigno Jr", "Son of Corazon\n& Benigno Jr"), fontface = "italic",
           colour = swatch("mauve"), size = 6.5 / ggplot2::.pt, lineheight = 0.9) +
  ## Duterte is the president-elect, labelled at the foot of the chart.
  annotate(
    "event_economist_2017", x = 2016.57, y = -21.6, yend = -62, label = "Duterte President Elect", hjust = 1,
    colour = tl_maroon, text_colour = tl_maroon, fontface = "bold", arrow = FALSE
  ) +
  ## The key.
  annotate("text", x = 1966, y = -33.8, label = "PRESIDENTS", hjust = 0, vjust = 1, colour = tl_maroon,
           fontface = "bold", size = 6.5 / ggplot2::.pt) +
  annotate("point", x = 1966.38, y = -47.7, shape = 25, size = 4.8 / ggplot2::.pt, fill = tl_maroon, colour = tl_maroon,
           stroke = 0) +
  annotate("text", x = 1967.37, y = -43, label = "Re-elected", hjust = 0, vjust = 1, colour = tl_maroon,
           size = 6.5 / ggplot2::.pt) +
  annotate("point", x = 1974.25, y = -38.1, shape = 21, size = 4.5 / ggplot2::.pt, fill = swatch("grey text"),
           colour = print_bg, stroke = 0.3) +
  annotate("text", x = 1974.84, y = -33.5, label = "Coup attempts", hjust = 0, vjust = 1,
           size = 6.5 / ggplot2::.pt) +
  coord_cartesian(xlim = c(1964.9, 2017.04), ylim = c(-64, 74), expand = FALSE, clip = "off") +
  labs(title = "The Philippines", subtitle = "Selected events", x = NULL, y = NULL,
       caption = "Source: The Economist") +
  theme_economist_2017("print", base_size = 7) +
  timeline_theme()
economist_2017_chart(philippines)
```

### Data timeline

```{r caliphate, econ_size = "two_column", econ_height = 265}
  annotate("point", x = caliphate_events$year, y = caliphate_events$to, colour = tl_maroon, size = 0.5) +
  geom_year_band_economist_2017(from = 1998, to = 2015, label_every = 1) +
  ## The key, in the subtitle line.
  annotate("rect", xmin = c(2002.2, 2003.9), xmax = c(2002.85, 2004.55), ymin = 6.55, ymax = 6.75,
           fill = c(tl_blue1, swatch("blue2"))) +
  annotate("text", x = c(2002.95, 2004.65), y = 6.87, label = c("Iraq", "Syria"), hjust = 0, vjust = 1,
           size = 7 / ggplot2::.pt) +
  coord_cartesian(xlim = c(1997.9, 2016.3), ylim = c(-4.2, 7.2), expand = FALSE, clip = "off") +
  labs(title = "Causation of a caliphate", subtitle = "Civilian death toll, ‘000:", x = NULL, y = NULL,
       caption = "Sources: Iraq Body Count; Violation Documentation Centre in Syria; The Economist") +
  theme_economist_2017("print", base_size = 7) +
  timeline_theme()
economist_2017_chart(caliphate)
```

### Data timeline with periods above

The same layers can sit above the data: here the bars of Putin's offices run
across the top, and the guide keys elections as dots on the year band.

```{r putin, econ_size = "two_column", econ_height = 240}

putin_events <- data.frame(
  year = c(2000.29, 2002.80, 2004.72, 2008.63, 2011.21, 2011.94, 2014.21, 2014.96),
  from = c(0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 4.35, 0, 0),
  to = c(93.83, 95.03, 94.51, 22.58, 93.48, 37.60, 114.40, 121.25),
  label = c(
    "Second\nChechen\nWar", "Moscow\nTheatre\nsiege", "Beslan\nSchool\nSiege", "Georgia war",
    "Start of Syrian\ncivil war", "Anti-\nGovernment\nProtests in\nBolotnaya", "Annexation\nof Crimea",
    "Rouble\ncollapses"
  ),
  hjust = c(0.5, 0.5, 0.5, 0, 0, 0, 1, 0)
)
putin_offices <- data.frame(
  start = c(1999.85, 2000.37, 2008.40, 2012.43),
  end = c(2000.35, 2008.37, 2012.40, 2016.47),
  label = c("PM", "PRESIDENT", "PRIME MINISTER", "PRESIDENT")
)
putin_elections <- data.frame(
  year = c(2003.97, 2007.97, 2011.98, 2000.24, 2004.22, 2008.20, 2012.22),
  type = rep(c("Presidential election", "Parliamentary election"), c(3, 4))
)
putin_election_cols <- c("Presidential election" = tl_blue1, "Parliamentary election" = swatch("mint"))

putin <- ggplot(putin_approval) +
  annotate(
    "span_economist_2017", xmin = 2008.54, xmax = 2009.64, ymin = 0.15, ymax = 97.34,
    label = "“Great recession”\nFinancial crisis; GDP shrinks 8%"
  ) +
  gridline_stubs(c(0, 25, 75, 100), 1999.27, 2017.33, 0.5, labels_left = NULL,
                 labels_right = c("0", "25", "75", "100")) +
  ## 50%, the line between approval and disapproval, runs across the chart.
  annotate("segment", x = 1999.27, xend = 2017.33, y = 50, yend = 50, colour = print_pal$text, linewidth = 0.1) +
  annotate("text", x = 2017.33, y = 50, label = "50", hjust = 1, vjust = -0.3, size = 6.5 / ggplot2::.pt) +
  geom_line(aes(month, government), colour = swatch("blue2"), linewidth = pt_line(1.5)) +
  geom_line(aes(month, putin), colour = tl_maroon, linewidth = pt_line(1.5)) +
  geom_event_economist_2017(aes(x = year, y = from, yend = to, label = label, hjust = hjust), data = putin_events) +
  geom_year_band_economist_2017(from = 2000, to = 2016, y = -1.4, height = 10, label_every = 1) +
  geom_point(aes(year, 1.7, colour = I(putin_election_cols[type])), data = putin_elections, size = 6 / ggplot2::.pt) +
  ## Putin's offices: across the top, labelled, and again below the band.
  geom_period_economist_2017(aes(xmin = start, xmax = end, y = 137.1, label = label), data = putin_offices,
                        size = 5.5 / ggplot2::.pt) +
  geom_period_economist_2017(aes(xmin = start, xmax = end, y = -13.05), data = putin_offices) +
  annotate("segment", x = c(2000.35, 2008.40, 2012.39), y = 122.97, yend = 137.11, colour = tl_maroon,
           linewidth = 0.1) +
  annotate("text", x = 1999.83, y = 146.3, label = "Putin is:", hjust = 0, vjust = 1, colour = tl_maroon,
           fontface = "bold", size = 6.5 / ggplot2::.pt) +
  annotate("text", x = c(2005.40, 2006.88), y = c(93.74, 69.41), label = c("Vladimir Putin", "Russian\ngovernment"),
           hjust = c(0, 0.5), vjust = 1, colour = c(tl_maroon, swatch("blue2 text")), size = 6.5 / ggplot2::.pt,
           lineheight = 0.9) +
  ## The key.
  annotate("point", x = 2013, y = c(162.7, 152.4), colour = putin_election_cols, size = 6 / ggplot2::.pt) +
  annotate("text", x = 2013.4, y = c(162.7, 152.4), label = names(putin_election_cols), hjust = 0,
           size = 6.5 / ggplot2::.pt) +
  coord_cartesian(xlim = c(1999.27, 2017.33), ylim = c(-17, 168), expand = FALSE, clip = "off") +
  labs(title = "I wanna be adored",
       subtitle = "Approval rating of Vladimir Putin and the Russian government, % polled",
       x = NULL, y = NULL, caption = "Sources: Levada Centre; The Economist") +
  theme_economist_2017("print", base_size = 7) +
  timeline_theme()
economist_2017_chart(putin)
```

### Mobile versions

> With often-lengthly [sic] text labels in fixed positions on the chart,
> timelines present a unique challenge for condensing to mobile.

The guide's example
comes in four versions: three columns for print, two for the web, and two
ways of fitting a phone: rotated to run down the screen, or compressed with
numbered labels listed below.

```{r mexico-data}
mexico_events <- data.frame(
  year = c(1823.2, 1874.8, 1913.4, 1928.4, 1937.5, 1982.0, 1993.6),
  label = c("First Mexican\nForeign Loan", "Porfirio Díaz\nBecomes President", "1914\nDefault", "1929\nCrash",
            "Mexican Oil\nNationalisation", "Debt\nCrisis", "Peso\nCrisis"),
  key = c(1, 2, NA, NA, 3, 4, 5)
)
mexico_wars <- data.frame(
  start = c(1846.4, 1857.9, 1861.8, 1910.2),
  end = c(1848.6, 1861.4, 1867.6, 1920.7),
  label = c("Mexican-\nAmerican war", "Reform\nwar", "French\noccupa-\ntion", "Mexican\nrevolution")
)
mexico_defaults <- data.frame(
  start = c(1827.5, 1832.5, 1843.5, 1853.6, 1865.6, 1913.4, 1928.3, 1982.0),
  end = c(1829.5, 1840.5, 1849.6, 1863.6, 1884.7, 1921.8, 1941.9, 1990.1)
)
war_fill <- "#B4DFEA" # C33.5 Y9, the guide's pale cyan for mexico_wars
default_note <- "*First new (non-restructured) bond issued for 50 years"
mexico_sources <- "Sources: Global Financial Data; Thomson Reuters; Haver Analytics"

## The chart common to print and web: the yield line on a log scale, wars as
## shaded spans, events from the axis, and the default periods on a track
## below the year labels.
mexican_waves <- function(media, event_top, war_labels, event_labels = mexico_events$label,
                          caption = mexico_sources) {
  ggplot(mexico_yields, aes(.data$year, .data$yield)) +
    annotate("rect", xmin = mexico_wars$start, xmax = mexico_wars$end, ymin = 0.52, ymax = 200, fill = war_fill) +
    geom_line(aes(group = .data$run), colour = tl_blue1, linewidth = pt_line(1)) +
    geom_event_economist_2017(
      aes(x = year, y = 0.52, yend = event_top, label = event_labels), data = mexico_events,
      inherit.aes = FALSE, colour = tl_maroon
    ) +
    annotate("text", x = war_labels$x, y = war_labels$y, label = mexico_wars$label, hjust = war_labels$hjust, vjust = 1,
             colour = swatch("blue2 text"), size = 6 / ggplot2::.pt, lineheight = 0.9) +
    annotate("text", x = 1961.6, y = 6.35, label = "*", size = 7 / ggplot2::.pt) +
    ## The default track, below the year labels, out of the panel.
    annotate("rect", xmin = 1820.8, xmax = 2015.8, ymin = 0.13, ymax = 0.185, fill = print_highlight) +
    geom_period_economist_2017(aes(xmin = start, xmax = end, y = 0.185), data = mexico_defaults, inherit.aes = FALSE,
                          fills = swatch("teal"), height = 5) +
    annotate("text", x = 1927.7, y = 0.12, label = "Periods of default on external debt", vjust = 1,
             colour = swatch("teal"), size = 6 / ggplot2::.pt) +
    annotate("text", x = 2015.6, y = 760, label = "log scale", hjust = 1, fontface = "italic",
             size = 6 / ggplot2::.pt) +
    scale_x_continuous(breaks = c(1824, seq(1830, 2010, 10), 2015), labels = economist_2017_year_format()) +
    scale_y_log10(breaks = c(1, 2, 4, 10, 20, 40, 100, 200, 400), position = "right",
                  guide = guide_axis_economist_2017()) +
    coord_cartesian(xlim = c(1820.8, 2017), ylim = c(0.52, 800), expand = FALSE, clip = "off") +
    labs(title = "Mexican waves", subtitle = "Mexico, selected government-bond mexico_yields, %",
         x = NULL, y = NULL, caption = caption) +
    theme_economist_2017(media, base_size = 7) +
    ## Room between the year labels and the source line for the default track.
    theme(axis.text.x = element_text(size = rel(0.8)), plot.caption = element_text(margin = margin(t = 30)))
}
```

The three-column print timeline:

```{r mexico-print, econ_size = "three_column", econ_height = 200}
mexico_print <- mexican_waves(
  "print", event_top = 650,
  war_labels = data.frame(x = c(1848.0, 1860.9, 1862.2, 1914.6), y = c(190, 190, 190, 190), hjust = c(1, 1, 0, 1))
)
economist_2017_chart(mexico_print, footnote = default_note)
```

The web desktop version, at two columns, staggers the war labels:

```{r mexico-web, econ_size = "two_column", econ_height = 215}
mexico_web <- mexican_waves(
  "web", event_top = c(650, 650, 650, 1400, 650, 650, 650),
  event_labels = replace(mexico_events$label, 4, "1929 Crash"),
  caption = "Sources: Global Financial Data;\nThomson Reuters; Haver Analytics",
  war_labels = data.frame(x = c(1848.6, 1857.9, 1862.4, 1919.2), y = c(190, 25, 170, 120), hjust = c(1, 1, 0, 1))
)
economist_2017_chart(mexico_web, "web", footnote = default_note)
```

Mobile option 1:

> Rotate timeline and run vertically on mobile. Works well where labels
> are relatively evenly spaced and where the data relates to specific
> labels, i.e. oil nationalisation in this example

```{r mexico-mobile-rotated, econ_size = "one_column", econ_height = 415}
mexico_rotated <- ggplot(mexico_yields, aes(yield, year)) +
  annotate("rect", ymin = mexico_wars$start, ymax = mexico_wars$end, xmin = 0.52, xmax = 200, fill = war_fill) +
  geom_path(aes(group = run), colour = tl_blue1, linewidth = pt_line(1)) +
  ## Events run across from the year axis to labels at the right.
  annotate("segment", x = 0.52, xend = 38, y = mexico_events$year, yend = mexico_events$year, colour = tl_maroon,
           linewidth = 0.18, arrow = grid::arrow(length = unit(2.5, "pt"), angle = 25, type = "closed")) +
  annotate("text", x = 45, y = mexico_events$year, label = sub("Becomes ", "Becomes\n", mexico_events$label),
           hjust = 0, vjust = 0.8,
           size = 6 / ggplot2::.pt, lineheight = 0.9) +
  annotate("text", x = c(1.6, 1.2, 1.3, 1.2), y = (mexico_wars$start + mexico_wars$end) / 2,
           label = c("Mexican-American war", "Reform war", "French occupation", "Mexican\nrevolution"),
           hjust = 0, colour = swatch("blue2 text"), size = 6 / ggplot2::.pt, lineheight = 0.9) +
  ## The default periods run down the left edge.
  annotate("rect", ymin = mexico_defaults$start, ymax = mexico_defaults$end, xmin = 0.2, xmax = 0.26,
           fill = swatch("teal")) +
  annotate("text", x = 0.2, y = 1811, label = "Periods of default on external debt", hjust = 0,
           colour = swatch("teal"), size = 6 / ggplot2::.pt) +
  scale_y_reverse(breaks = c(1824, seq(1840, 2000, 10), 2015), labels = economist_2017_year_format()) +
  scale_x_log10(breaks = c(1, 10, 100), position = "top",
                sec.axis = dup_axis(), guide = guide_axis(cap = "both")) +
  coord_cartesian(xlim = c(0.2, 500), ylim = c(2018, 1820), expand = FALSE, clip = "off") +
  labs(title = "Mexican waves", subtitle = "Mexico, selected government-bond mexico_yields, %",
       x = NULL, y = NULL, caption = "Sources: Global Financial Data;\nThomson Reuters; Haver Analytics") +
  theme_economist_2017("web", base_size = 7) +
  theme(panel.grid.major = element_blank(), axis.text.y = element_text(hjust = 0))
economist_2017_chart(mexico_rotated, "web")
```

```{r mexico-mobile-key}
## The numbered events, listed below the chart.
key_badge <- function(n) {
  sprintf(
    paste0(
      '<span style="display:inline-block;width:9pt;height:9pt;border-radius:50%%;background:%s;',
      'color:white;font-weight:700;font-size:6pt;line-height:9pt;text-align:center">%d</span>'
    ),
    tl_maroon, n
  )
}
gt::gt(data.frame(key = mexico_numbered$key, event = gsub("\n", " ", mexico_numbered$label)), id = "mexico-key") |>
  gt::text_transform(fn = function(x) key_badge(as.integer(x)), locations = gt::cells_body(columns = key)) |>
  gt::tab_options(
    column_labels.hidden = TRUE, table.width = "160pt", table.font.size = "7pt", table.margin.left = "0",
    table.border.top.style = "none", table.border.bottom.style = "none", data_row.padding = "1.5pt",
    table_body.hlines.color = "white", table_body.hlines.width = "2pt"
  ) |>
  gt::opt_table_font(font = econ_table_font) |>
  gt::tab_style(gt::cell_fill(color = print_highlight), gt::cells_body()) |>
  gt::cols_width(key ~ "16pt") |>
  gt::tab_source_note(econ_source(
    "Sources: Global Financial Data;<br>Thomson Reuters;<br>Haver Analytics",
    "*First new<br>(non-restructured)<br>bond issued for 50 years"
  ))
```

## Miscellaneous styling

### Number boxes

> Use where multiple charts are referenced in text

A 7.5pt bold numeral on the number-box fill, top right.

```{r number-box, econ_height = 165}
numbered <- tokyo +
  labs(caption = NULL)

economist_2017_chart(
  numbered +
    labs(caption = "Source: Thomson Reuters"),
  media = "print",
  number = 1
)
```

### Highlight panels

> For secondary information, like forecast or estimate, use neutral style

```{r highlight-neutral, econ_height = 165}
## Five-year intervals; every country is 100 in 2015.
jobs <- data.frame(
  year = rep(seq(1950, 2100, by = 5), 4),
  place = rep(c("Japan", "United States", "European Union", "China"), each = 31),
  index = c(
    65, 71, 77, 86, 93, 98, 102, 106, 111, 112, 111, 109, 105, 100, 96, 93, 89, 85, 79, 75, 72, 69, 67, 65, 63, 62, 60,
    59, 58, 56, 56,
    48, 50, 53, 56, 61, 66, 71, 75, 78, 83, 89, 94, 97, 100, 101, 102, 102, 104, 106, 108, 110, 111, 112, 113, 115, 116,
    117, 118, 119, 119, 119,
    76, 78, 80, 83, 85, 88, 91, 95, 97, 98, 99, 101, 102, 100, 98, 96, 94, 91, 89, 87, 85, 83, 82, 81, 81, 80, 79, 78,
    77, 76, 76,
    34, 35, 36, 39, 45, 51, 58, 67, 75, 81, 86, 94, 99, 100, 100, 98, 96, 90, 86, 83, 79, 73, 69, 67, 65, 63, 59, 57,
    55, 54, 53
  )
)
jobs$place <- factor(jobs$place, levels = c("China", "European Union", "Japan", "United States"))
## Four labels set in the panel, as in the guide, in place of a key.
job_labels <- data.frame(
  year = c(1971, 2029, 2095, 1989), index = c(112, 115, 91, 49),
  label = c("Japan", "United\nStates", "European\nUnion", "China")
)

fill_jobs <- ggplot(jobs, aes(year, index, colour = place)) +
  ## The forecast panel: neutral fill, with a 1pt rule across its top.
  annotate("rect", xmin = 2015, xmax = 2100, ymin = -Inf, ymax = 137, fill = print_highlight) +
  annotate("segment", x = 2015, xend = 2100, y = 137, yend = 137, colour = swatch("grey box"), linewidth = 0.35) +
  annotate("text", x = 2058, y = 130.5, label = "FORECAST", size = 6.5 / ggplot2::.pt,
           colour = swatch("grey box")) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 100, colour = econ_red, linewidth = 0.2) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.6) +
  geom_text(data = job_labels, aes(year, index, label = label), colour = print_pal$text, size = 7 / ggplot2::.pt,
            lineheight = 0.9, inherit.aes = FALSE) +
  ## The 5pt black circle on the index point.
  geom_point(data = data.frame(year = 2015, index = 100), aes(year, index), colour = "black",
             size = 5 / 0.75 / ggplot2::.pt, stroke = 0, inherit.aes = FALSE) +
  scale_y_continuous(guide = guide_axis_economist_2017(), position = "right", limits = c(20, 137),
                     breaks = seq(20, 120, 20), expand = c(0, 0)) +
  scale_x_continuous(limits = c(1933, 2141), expand = c(0, 0), breaks = seq(1950, 2100, 25),
                     minor_breaks = seq(1950, 2100, 5), labels = economist_2017_year_format(),
                     guide = guide_axis(minor.ticks = TRUE)) +
  scale_colour_economist_2017("print", type = "line_side") +
  labs(
    title = "Who will fill the jobs?",
    subtitle = "Working-age population*, 2015=100",
    x = NULL, y = NULL
  ) +
  theme_economist_2017("print", base_size = 7) +
  theme(legend.position = "none")

economist_2017_chart(
  fill_jobs +
    labs(caption = "Source: United Nations\nPopulation Division"),
  media = "print",
  footnote = "*Aged 15-64"
)
```

> For highlights that are central to the message of the chart, use colour

A 30% tint of the guide's red.

```{r highlight-colour, econ_height = 155}
## The guide's line, at half-monthly intervals.
merkel <- data.frame(
  t = seq(2005, 2016.25, by = 1 / 24),
  approval = c(
    61, 61, 60, 62, 65, 67, 71, 73, 79, 76, 74, 72, 71, 70, 69, 67, 65, 63, 60, 58, 56, 55, 55, 55, 53, 51, 51,
    48, 53, 54, 56, 58, 60, 61, 61, 62, 65, 65, 65, 68, 70, 70, 71, 72, 72, 73, 75, 75, 76, 76, 76, 75, 74, 72,
    70, 70, 68, 67, 69, 69, 68, 67, 68, 69, 69, 69, 70, 69, 70, 67, 70, 68, 67, 65, 64, 66, 66, 67, 68, 70, 66,
    70, 67, 66, 67, 68, 66, 66, 66, 64, 65, 66, 66, 67, 69, 69, 70, 71, 71, 71, 71, 71, 71, 71, 71, 70, 70, 68,
    65, 65, 64, 61, 60, 61, 60, 56, 61, 57, 54, 53, 52, 49, 46, 45, 42, 44, 44, 47, 44, 44, 43, 42, 42, 45, 47,
    48, 49, 51, 52, 52, 52, 49, 52, 49, 49, 50, 51, 50, 50, 48, 47, 47, 46, 46, 47, 50, 52, 52, 53, 56, 58, 59,
    59, 62, 63, 63, 63, 63, 62, 62, 61, 60, 59, 61, 62, 63, 65, 67, 62, 67, 62, 64, 65, 67, 64, 61, 67, 61, 65,
    67, 67, 69, 70, 69, 67, 67, 66, 67, 69, 66, 69, 68, 67, 68, 68, 68, 69, 69, 68, 68, 68, 68, 68, 69, 68, 69,
    69, 70, 70, 71, 71, 69, 68, 68, 66, 67, 69, 70, 71, 72, 73, 74, 73, 72, 71, 70, 69, 68, 68, 70, 68, 69, 70,
    71, 71, 72, 72, 74, 72, 71, 69, 68, 67, 67, 67, 66, 65, 63, 61, 59, 56, 53, 52, 50, 53, 55, 58, 55, 50, 49,
    46
  )
)
## Message-critical highlight: c10 m70 y50 at a 30% tint, with a 1pt rule on top.
crisis_tint <- "#F4C7C5"
crisis_ink <- swatch("red1")
crisis_rules <- data.frame(xmin = c(2009.56, 2015.48), xmax = c(2012.27, 2016.24))

## The chart for either medium: the highlight tint, the colour of its rule and
## label, and the line's colour.
malaise_plot <- function(tint, ink, line, media) {
  ggplot(merkel, aes(.data$t, .data$approval)) +
    geom_rect(data = crisis_rules, aes(xmin = .data$xmin, xmax = .data$xmax, ymin = -Inf, ymax = 80),
              inherit.aes = FALSE, fill = tint) +
    geom_segment(data = crisis_rules, aes(x = .data$xmin, xend = .data$xmax, y = 80, yend = 80),
                 inherit.aes = FALSE, colour = ink, linewidth = 0.35) +
    annotate("text", x = 2010.9, y = 74.5, label = "Euro\nCrisis", size = 7.5 / ggplot2::.pt,
             colour = ink, lineheight = 0.9) +
    annotate("text", x = 2015.83, y = 35, label = "Migrant\nCrisis", size = 7.5 / ggplot2::.pt,
             colour = ink, lineheight = 0.9) +
    geom_hline(yintercept = 50, colour = "black", linewidth = 0.2) +
    geom_line(colour = line, linewidth = 0.6) +
    geom_scale_break_economist_2017() +
    scale_y_continuous(guide = guide_axis_economist_2017(), position = "right", limits = c(24, 80),
                       breaks = seq(30, 80, 10), expand = c(0, 0)) +
    scale_x_continuous(limits = c(2003.8, 2018.3), expand = c(0, 0),
                       breaks = c(2005, 2007, 2009, 2011, 2013, 2015, 2016),
                       minor_breaks = 2005:2016, labels = economist_2017_year_format(),
                       guide = guide_axis(minor.ticks = TRUE, cap = "upper")) +
    labs(
      title = "Mutti's malaise",
      subtitle = "German approval of Angela\nMerkel, % polled",
      x = NULL, y = NULL
    ) +
    theme_economist_2017(media, base_size = 7)
}

malaise <- malaise_plot(crisis_tint, crisis_ink, pal_line(1), "print")

economist_2017_chart(
  malaise +
    labs(caption = "Source: ARD DeutschlandTREND/infratest dimap"),
  media = "print"
)
```

> For web-only charts, use print bkgd colour for highlights

The same chart on white, with the panels in the print background blue.

```{r highlight-web, econ_height = 155}
## Web charts use the print palette; only the highlight changes, to the print background.
malaise_web <- malaise_plot(tint = print_pal$ground, ink = crisis_ink, line = pal_line(1), media = "web")

economist_2017_chart(
  malaise_web +
    labs(caption = "Source: ARD DeutschlandTREND/infratest dimap"),
  media = "web"
)
```

### Highlight labels

> Use to mark specific dates and points on axis

A 0.5pt red rule with a 7pt label.

> If there are only 1 or 2 points, and they are key to the chart meaning,
> use colour/medium font

```{r highlight-labels, econ_height = 155}
## The guide's line, at weekly intervals.
toshiba <- data.frame(
  t = seq(2015, by = 1 / 60, length.out = 122),
  price = c(
    510, 505, 495, 485, 475, 470, 475, 480, 485, 490, 490, 485, 480, 500, 510, 515, 500, 490, 490, 490, 485,
    460, 450, 425, 420, 430, 440, 440, 435, 430, 415, 400, 385, 380, 380, 380, 375, 375, 380, 375, 365, 345,
    335, 320, 315, 315, 320, 330, 340, 340, 340, 330, 315, 300, 290, 295, 300, 290, 260, 255, 235, 240, 230,
    220, 210, 200, 185, 180, 170, 180, 190, 195, 200, 195, 205, 210, 210, 220, 235, 240, 230, 225, 225, 230,
    245, 260, 275, 290, 285, 285, 280, 285, 290, 295, 285, 275, 265, 280, 285, 305, 320, 330, 320, 320, 330,
    340, 355, 360, 370, 380, 375, 380, 385, 395, 410, 430, 445, 460, 425, 360, 335, 270
  )
)
## Each event: a 0.5pt rule from the labelled point down to the axis, and its label.
events <- data.frame(
  t = c(2015.396, 2015.542, 2015.983, 2016.31, 2016.967),
  top = c(653, 518, 431, 245, 624),
  label = c("Accounting\nscandal", "CEO resigns", "$4.6bn\nrecord loss", "Westinghouse\nWrite-down",
            "CB&I Stone\n& Webster\nwrite-down"),
  ## Labels right of their rules, except the fourth (below) and the last (centred).
  lx = c(2015.436, 2015.582, 2016.023, 2016.12, 2016.86),
  ly = c(653, 518, 431, 150, 712),
  hjust = c(0, 0, 0, 0, 0.5),
  vjust = c(1, 1, 1, 0.5, 0.5)
)

woes_chart <- ggplot(toshiba, aes(t, price)) +
  geom_segment(data = events, aes(x = t, xend = t, y = 0, yend = top), colour = crisis_ink, linewidth = 0.234,
               inherit.aes = FALSE) +
  geom_point(data = events, aes(t, top), colour = crisis_ink, size = 0.9, stroke = 0, inherit.aes = FALSE) +
  geom_label(data = events, aes(lx, ly, label = label, hjust = hjust, vjust = vjust), fill = print_bg,
             size = 7 / ggplot2::.pt, linewidth = 0, label.padding = unit(0.1, "lines"), lineheight = 0.9,
             inherit.aes = FALSE) +
  geom_line(colour = pal_line(1), linewidth = 0.8) +
  coord_cartesian(ylim = c(0, 650), clip = "off") +
  scale_y_continuous(guide = guide_axis_economist_2017(), position = "right", breaks = seq(0, 600, 100),
                     expand = c(0, 0)) +
  scale_x_continuous(limits = c(2014.89, 2017.46), expand = c(0, 0), breaks = c(2015.5, 2016.5, 2017.06),
                     minor_breaks = seq(2015, 2017, by = 1 / 12), labels = c("2015", "16", "17"),
                     guide = guide_axis(minor.ticks = TRUE)) +
  labs(
    title = "Westinghouse woes",
    subtitle = "Toshiba, share price, yen",
    x = NULL, y = NULL
  ) +
  theme_economist_2017("print", base_size = 7)

economist_2017_chart(
  woes_chart +
    labs(caption = "Source: Thomson Reuters"),
  media = "print"
)
```

### Index charts

> 0.5pt red line on index line

> 5pt diameter black circle on index point

```{r index-chart, econ_height = 165}
## One value a year.
income <- data.frame(
  year = rep(1979:2013, 3),
  measure = factor(rep(c("Market income", "plus transfers", "plus transfers less taxes"), each = 35),
                   levels = c("Market income", "plus transfers", "plus transfers less taxes")),
  index = c(
    100, 97.5, 96.5, 94.6, 93.9, 98.8, 99.9, 102.2, 103.1, 104.9, 106.5, 105.5, 103.7, 103.7, 103.7,
    105.4, 108.9, 110.3, 113.5, 118.3, 121.7, 122.2, 121.6, 118.1, 117.9, 121.5, 123.8, 126.5, 129.7,
    124.7, 118.3, 117.9, 116.7, 116.9, 119.4,
    100, 96.1, 96.1, 97.1, 97.2, 101.9, 102.4, 105.2, 106.6, 108, 109.8, 109.8, 109.5, 109.9, 110.5,
    112.7, 116, 117.9, 120.8, 125.6, 129.1, 130.7, 134.6, 133.5, 135.7, 139.5, 142.7, 145.4, 148.9, 148.5,
    147.5, 147.7, 147.1, 147, 147.1,
    100, 97.1, 97.1, 96.1, 95.5, 100.5, 101.3, 103.9, 105.1, 106.5, 108.5, 108.5, 108.1, 108.3, 108.9,
    110.7, 114.1, 116.1, 118.6, 122.7, 126.1, 127.1, 128.7, 126.8, 127.5, 131.6, 134.7, 137.3, 140.5,
    136.8, 134.9, 135.5, 133.9, 134.5, 136.3
  )
)

pain <- ggplot(income, aes(year, index, colour = measure)) +
  ## 0.5pt red line on the index line, and a 5pt black circle on the index point.
  geom_hline(yintercept = 100, colour = econ_red, linewidth = 0.234) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.8) +
  geom_point(data = data.frame(year = 1979, index = 100), aes(year, index), colour = "black",
             size = 5 / 0.75 / ggplot2::.pt, stroke = 0, inherit.aes = FALSE) +
  scale_y_continuous(guide = guide_axis_economist_2017(), position = "right", limits = c(90, 150),
                     breaks = seq(90, 150, 10), expand = c(0, 0)) +
  scale_x_continuous(limits = c(1976.8, 2018.2), expand = c(0, 0),
                     breaks = c(1979, 1985, 1990, 1995, 2000, 2005, 2010, 2013), minor_breaks = 1979:2013,
                     labels = economist_2017_year_format(),
                     guide = guide_axis(minor.ticks = TRUE)) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c(pal_line(4)[1], pal_dot(6)[6], pal_line(4)[4])) +
  labs(
    title = "Easing the pain",
    subtitle = "United States, median real\nhousehold income*, 1979=100",
    x = NULL, y = NULL, colour = NULL
  ) +
  theme_economist_2017("print", base_size = 7) +
  guides(colour = guide_legend(nrow = 2, byrow = TRUE))

economist_2017_chart(
  pain +
    labs(caption = "Source: CBO"),
  media = "print",
  footnote = "*Adjusted for household size"
)
```

### Truncated year labels

Dated axes truncate years to two digits, keeping the first label and each century boundary in full: `1948 52 56 ... 96 2000 04`. `economist_2017_year_format()` does this.

```{r year-labels}
economist_2017_year(seq(1948, 2016, 4))
```

### Broken scales

> Use when breaking y-axis on line, thermometer and scatter charts
> not needed on indexed, negative scale or inverted scales

> DON’T BREAK SCALE ON BAR/COLUMN CHARTS - USE THERMOMETER INSTEAD

Truncate the axis with `limits`, then add `geom_scale_break_economist_2017()`.

```{r broken-scale, econ_height = 155}
broken <- ggplot(merkel, aes(t, approval)) +
  geom_line(colour = pal_line(1), linewidth = 0.8) +
  ## Black, 0.4pt, 6pt wide, between the baseline and the lowest tick.
  geom_scale_break_economist_2017() +
  scale_y_continuous(guide = guide_axis_economist_2017(), position = "right", limits = c(24, 80),
                     breaks = seq(30, 80, 10), expand = c(0, 0)) +
  scale_x_continuous(limits = c(2003.8, 2018.3), expand = c(0, 0),
                     breaks = c(2005, 2007, 2009, 2011, 2013, 2015, 2016),
                     minor_breaks = 2005:2016, labels = economist_2017_year_format(),
                     guide = guide_axis(minor.ticks = TRUE, cap = "upper")) +
  labs(
    title = "Mutti's malaise",
    subtitle = "German approval of Angela\nMerkel, % polled",
    x = NULL, y = NULL
  ) +
  theme_economist_2017("print", base_size = 7)

economist_2017_chart(
  broken +
    labs(caption = "Source: ARD DeutschlandTREND/infratest dimap"),
  media = "print"
)
```
